Under Edwards' leadership, who holds the record as the highest run-scorer in T20 internationals for both men and women, England efficiently managed the game against lackluster opposition. Edwards skillfully balanced accumulating runs with aggressive play, especially after England lost Sarah Taylor and Heather Knight in quick succession, adding only one run in between.At a precarious 71-3, Edwards found support in Nat Sciver, who contributed 27 in a 47-run partnership. Late in the innings, Danni Wyatt and Brunt added a powerful surge, scoring 35 in the final three overs. Bangladesh, who had never scored more than 115 in a T20 international, struggled from the outset. Sharmin Akhter was bowled by the formidable Brunt in the first over, leaving England firmly in control.Although Nigar Sultana and Salma Khatun set a Bangladesh record with a 64-run stand for the fifth wicket, the match was already beyond their reach. text: Wales women's footballer Jess Fishlock says more must be done to provide an environment in which gay players feel comfortable to come out. Jess Fishlock, 29, has openly discussed the hurdles she has encountered as a prominent gay athlete. In the Premier League, no current players have come out as gay. However, a recent BBC survey indicates that 82% of fans would not have an issue with a gay player. Fishlock emphasized the importance of context and support, stating, The environment and the timing is so important. That's what we have to get - the environment to say 'it's ok and it's not a problem'. That's what we're fighting for and what we've got to work on.Speaking to BBC Radio Wales Sport, she expressed concern over the potential negative impact if a footballer were to come out for the wrong reasons. What you do want is for them to feel comfortable that they can come out, they can be themselves and they're happy with that, she said.In February 2014, Casey Stoney, the former England women's captain, publicly came out, becoming the most high-profile active gay footballer in England. She noted that homosexuality is more accepted in women's football compared to men's.Justin Fashanu was the first male player in England to come out as gay in 1990. Tragically, he took his own life at 37 in 1998, and since then, no male professional player has come out during their career in England.Fishlock, who plays for Seattle Reign and is currently on loan to Melbourne City, has faced abuse for her sexuality but takes pride in inspiring others to embrace their identity. I've had people write letters telling how me being so open and so happy and so comfortable with who I am at the highest level at a huge sport has actually made them realise it's ok and they don't have to commit suicide or they don't have these dark thoughts anymore, she shared. Launched by LGBT equality charity Stonewall in 2013, the Rainbow Laces campaign seeks to combat homophobic, biphobic, and transphobic attitudes in sports. Premier League matches will feature rainbow flags, referees will don rainbow-colored laces, and Fishlock has voiced her support for the campaign's objectives.

text: Eastern Ukraine has become a testing ground for Russia's new military capabilities. In 2008, Russia's military engagement in Georgia initially appeared as a straightforward victory. However, the performance of Russian forces in key aspects of modern warfare deeply troubled the country's generals. Over the past seven years, Russia has embarked on an ambitious campaign to rearm, re-equip, and retrain its military to address these shortcomings and narrow the capability gap with Western armies. The fruits of these efforts are now evident in eastern Ukraine, where pro-Russian separatists have been making significant advances against Ukrainian government troops. Unlike Russia, Ukraine has not undergone a similar modernization process, leaving its military at a disadvantage when confronting the advanced weaponry and systems supplied by Russia.Two critical areas where Russia has made significant advancements are in the deployment of UAVs (drones) for surveillance and targeting, and in electronic warfare. Identified as weaknesses in 2008, Russia has since developed these technologies extensively. Their widespread use in eastern Ukraine now puts Ukrainian government forces at a severe disadvantage.A major issue for Ukrainian forces is their lack of secure communication systems. This vulnerability makes their communications susceptible to jamming and reveals their locations to Russian direction-finding equipment, leading to rapid targeting by Russian artillery, including powerful systems like the Grad rocket launchers.Although the US has provided non-lethal aid, including special radar to detect incoming mortar fire, the effectiveness of this technology is hampered by communication challenges. Moreover, Ukraine has yet to receive advanced systems capable of pinpointing the source of long-range artillery fire.The situation is further exacerbated by the arrival of modern tanks from Russia, which outclass the older Ukrainian models. Ukraine also suffers from a shortage of effective anti-armour weaponry. To enhance their forces' survivability against Russian military advances, Ukraine has requested support that includes these systems, along with medical and field hospital equipment.The loss of Ukrainian aircraft in the conflict zone highlights the robust air defense capabilities of the Russian-backed separatists. Their arsenal includes not only the Buk missile system, implicated in the downing of Malaysia Airlines flight MH17, but also other systems like Strela for lower altitudes, and a variety of lighter, shoulder-launched missiles.Despite Russian denials, independent experts, NATO, Western leaders, and the Kiev government assert there is clear evidence of direct Russian military involvement. As part of its military overhaul, Russia has been conducting extensive exercises and maneuvers, involving tens of thousands of servicemen, with scenarios often hostile towards the West.Eastern Ukraine now serves as a live testing ground for Russia's new weapons, systems, and tactics. The outcomes of these tests, particularly against any potential US defensive systems supplied to Ukraine, will provide Russia with valuable insights into how its forces might perform in a direct confrontation with NATO.Keir Giles, an analyst with the Conflict Studies Research Centre in Oxford and an Associate Fellow with the Russia and Eurasia Programme at Chatham House in London, offers insight into these developments.

text: A smartphone app is as effective at testing eyesight as an optician's clinic, a trial suggests. A groundbreaking innovation from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine could revolutionize eye care for millions in remote regions worldwide. Researchers have developed a smartphone-based eye examination kit, the Portable Eye Examination Kit (Peek), which has shown promising results in trials involving 233 participants in Kenya, as reported in JAMA Ophthalmology. This innovative approach yielded results comparable to traditional eye charts.Globally, over 285 million individuals suffer from blindness or visual impairment, often due to conditions that are easily treatable with glasses or cataract surgery. However, many remain out of reach of even basic eye exams. To address this, the London team, collaborating with Scottish colleagues, adapted a smartphone to perform a series of eye tests requiring minimal training and offering high portability.Peek employs the phone's camera to scan for cataracts and utilizes its flash to examine the eye's interior for diseases. Its Acuity App features a shrinking letter on the screen, serving as a basic vision test. Initial clinical data from Kenya confirmed that this vision test matched the accuracy of conventional eye charts. Participants underwent examinations both at home and in clinics, with further compelling results on retinal scanning soon to be published.Dr. Andrew Bastawrous, leading the project, explained to the BBC: The main reason for most people not getting eye treatment is simply that they don't access the services and that's usually because the services are so far away from them or are unaffordable. If we can detect people with visual impairment much earlier on, then we have a much greater chance of increasing awareness and ensuring they have appropriate treatment. So something as simple as a vision test can be part of that journey.Costing around £300, this smartphone solution is significantly cheaper than traditional eye examination equipment, which can exceed £100,000. The International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness heralds the app as a potential game changer, noting the scarcity of trained eye health staff in impoverished areas. The tool allows relatively untrained individuals to administer eye care services.However, even if widespread testing becomes feasible, a significant challenge remains: funding the treatment for millions in need.

text: Three men and a woman are trapped and four people have been taken to hospital after three explosions at a wood treatment works near Macclesfield. A devastating incident unfolded at Wood Flour Mills on Tunstall Road in Bosley when a four-storey building collapsed at 09:10 BST, igniting large fires, according to the fire service. Describing the site as a scene of devastation, the fire service reported that a search team would enter the site at dawn. Cheshire East Council confirmed that the blast has left 50 workers jobless. Meanwhile, Cheshire Police stated that 35 individuals present at the scene were evaluated, with four treated for breathing difficulties and another four transported to hospitals in Birmingham, Merseyside, and Stoke. A 29-year-old woman suffered severe burns and blast injuries to her head, face, arms, and chest, as reported by West Midlands Ambulance Service. She was airlifted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham for treatment.Assistant Chief Constable Guy Hindle of Cheshire Police commented, Four people remain unaccounted for, and urban search and rescue teams are assessing the scene to determine if it is safe to enter the property to locate them. We are in contact with the families of the missing individuals.Earlier reports from firefighters indicated the possibility of further explosions. Steve Barnes from Cheshire Fire and Rescue Service described the scene as hazardous, emphasizing the need to secure the area for potential rescue operations. Chief Fire Officer Paul Hancock added, We are dealing with four missing individuals, believed to be within the building. We aim to address this once the incident is fully controlled.Plans for a search team to enter the site at first light on Saturday are underway, though portions of the building remain ablaze. The structure houses dangerous materials such as heating oil, kerosene, acetylene, and asbestos, along with a silo containing highly flammable wood flour used in wood laminate flooring production.The North West Ambulance Service (NWAS) dispatched six ambulances and two rapid response vehicles, with an air ambulance also present. An NWAS spokesperson noted, Two patients were taken to Royal Stoke University Hospital, and one to Whiston Hospital in Merseyside.Emergency services have yet to determine the cause of the fire. Patrick Jones, a shift worker who left the site just hours before the explosion, expressed concern for his colleagues, stating, I am still worried about my mates. There are four of them that are still missing. He was unable to pass through the police cordon.Authorities warned that smoke drifted northeast, advising residents as far as 15 miles away in Wildboarclough to keep doors and windows shut. At Bosley St Mary's C of E Primary School, located about a mile from the explosion, over 40 pupils were kept indoors. Headteacher Raj Barard recounted, We heard and felt the explosion just after 09:00 BST. Police instructed us to keep the children inside. It felt like an earthquake.BBC Radio Manchester's Jonathan Ali reported that six hours post-explosion, smoke continued to linger over the factory. Angela Shuker, residing near the mill, noted, Our doors banged, and we saw flames rising close by. Charli Alston, 18, witnessed the explosion while walking her dog, saying, There was a huge bang, like thunder, followed by massive flames.Electricity North West confirmed that power was cut to 165 homes in Bosley to ensure firefighter safety, with most homes now reconnected. text: Organisers of this summer's music festivals have been asked by the government to warn about legal highs. In a bid to curb the dangers posed by new psychoactive substances at festivals, Minister for Crime Prevention James Brokenshire has reached out to festival organisers, urging them to alert attendees about the potential risks of these substances. Brokenshire emphasized the need for vigilance, particularly as these drugs are often marketed as legal or herbal, during the festival season. In his initiative, Brokenshire has also communicated with councils and police forces in festival regions, stressing the importance of collaboration to disseminate the message that these substances are not necessarily safe and may even contain illegal drugs. He stated, We are going to change our drug laws so we can respond quickly to emerging substances by introducing a temporary ban while we seek full scientific advice.The minister's plan includes modifying drug legislation to enable temporary bans on these emerging substances while awaiting comprehensive scientific evaluation. This move follows the recent reclassification of several substances previously sold as legal highs, such as mephedrone, which is now a Class B drug.The Home Office has highlighted concerns about substances like naphyrone, often marketed under the name NRG1 and sold as plant food or bath salts, which may actually contain illegal drugs. However, the government has assured that no substance will face a permanent ban without thorough assessment from the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs.In his letter to festival organisers, Brokenshire urged them to reassess their safety measures to protect the public, especially young people, from the potential dangers associated with all drugs. As part of your preparations for this year's event, I ask you to review the measures you have put in place to ensure that your festival is as safe an environment as possible, he wrote.The government's proactive stance has been applauded by Melvin Benn, managing director of Festival Republic, which runs the Latitude, Big Chill, and Reading and Leeds Festivals. Benn affirmed, I can confirm that we do not allow legal high traders to trade at any Festival Republic festival and fully support the minister's view.

text: The leader of Colombia's largest armed rebel group, the Farc, has said he ordered the organisation in September to stop buying guns and ammunition. Rodrigo Londono Echeverri, widely known as Timochenko, emphasized the Farc's dedication to reducing hostilities with the Colombian army through a recent decision. For nearly three years, the left-wing group and the Colombian government have been immersed in peace negotiations. Both parties anticipate signing an agreement by March.Since the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia began their armed struggle in 1964, an estimated 220,000 people have lost their lives. The peace talks, initiated in Havana, Cuba, in November 2012, aim to transition the rebels from armed conflict to participating in the legal political process.Timochenko's declaration was made in a tweet directed at Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos. The negotiations have reached consensus on four key issues: the political involvement of the rebels, land rights, drug trafficking, and, most recently, transitional justice. The latter, concerning the punishment of rebels who committed crimes, was considered one of the most challenging topics.On September 23, when both parties announced an agreement on transitional justice, President Santos traveled to Cuba. There, he shook hands with Timochenko for the first time and set a six-month deadline—until March 23, 2016—for finalizing a peace agreement. The rebels have expressed a desire to sign the deal even earlier.However, several issues and the implementation of the agreement remain under discussion. Any final deal will require approval through a Colombian referendum. Last month, President Santos expressed his readiness to join the Farc in a bilateral ceasefire starting January 1, 2016, contingent on significant progress in the talks. The rebels have already declared a truce.Additionally, Santos has halted radio and television campaigns aimed at encouraging rebels to leave the Farc, describing this as a gesture of goodwill. Such demobilization campaigns are typically intensified in the weeks leading up to Christmas.

text: You may not have heard of Judith Hill, but you've almost certainly heard her voice. Judith Hill, a renowned Californian singer, has graced the stage with some of the most iconic names in music, providing backing vocals for legends like Stevie Wonder, Elton John, Josh Groban, Carole King, Robbie Williams, and Rod Stewart. Her career reached a pivotal moment in 2009 when she was set to be a featured singer on Michael Jackson's ill-fated This Is It tour. Her mesmerizing duet with Jackson is immortalized in the rehearsal film released posthumously.Hill's journey continued with a stint on the US version of The Voice, where her unexpected elimination led judge Adam Levine to famously exclaim, I hate this country. Her attempts to forge a solo career were documented in the Oscar-winning film 20 Feet From Stardom, which highlighted the often-overlooked contributions of mainly African-American backup singers to the rock music industry.The turning point in Hill's solo career came when Prince, having read about her in a newspaper, invited her to record at his Paisley Park Studios in Minneapolis. In an interview with the BBC, Hill shared insights into their collaboration, her experiences as a backing singer, and her memories of the day Michael Jackson passed away.When asked about her earliest musical memory, Hill recalled Walk With Me by Vanessa Bell Armstrong. She credits her mother as the first to recognize her singing talent, recounting how they wrote their first song together when she was just four years old.Landing a spot on Michael Jackson's tour came after a small gig in Los Angeles, where connections with musicians led to an audition with Jackson's musical director. Hill was soon hired, leaving her job at a clothing store to join the tour. She remembers the advice Jackson gave her about seizing every moment on stage, admiring how he painted vivid pictures with his lyrics and movements.Reflecting on the day Jackson died, Hill described the surreal experience of being at a restaurant when the news broke. Initially dismissing the rumors, reality hit when she arrived at the Staples Center for rehearsal, only to find the stage being dismantled. Singing at Jackson's memorial service was overwhelming, taking place on the same stage they had rehearsed on just weeks before.Her experience on The Voice taught Hill about her vocal identity, revealing her innate soul singer roots. The film 20 Feet From Stardom, which resonated widely, brought new opportunities and recognition to her career.Transitioning to a solo artist was challenging, but Hill's passion for music kept her going. She explained the difference between backing vocals and fronting her own material, emphasizing the increased responsibility and creative control she enjoys as a solo artist.Among the artists she's worked with, Natalie Cole stood out as the most demanding, with precise expectations for her singers. Hill's collaboration with Prince began after she named him as her dream collaborator in an interview. Prince personally reached out, leading to a creative partnership at Paisley Park.Prince's sense of humor was evident in a prank call where he impersonated someone else. His contribution to her album was significant, involving production, arrangement, and collaboration on grooves and edits. Hill titled the album Back In Time to evoke the golden era of funk and soul, drawing on her childhood and musical upbringing. The song Angel In The Dark holds special meaning for Hill, symbolizing divine intervention during her darkest times.Judith Hill's debut album, Back In Time, is now available on NPG Records.

text: Egyptians go to the polls on 26 and 27 May to elect a new president. Anticipated results on June 5 are expected to confirm a decisive victory for former defense minister Abdul Fattah al-Sisi in Egypt's presidential election. The only contender against him is veteran left-wing politician and previous presidential candidate, Hamdeen Sabahi.The election is taking place earlier than planned due to the military's removal of Islamist President Mohammed Morsi following widespread protests last July. This move initiated a roadmap to democracy, initially scheduling presidential elections two years in advance. Although parliamentary elections were intended to precede the presidential vote, the interim government reversed this order in January. Consequently, parliamentary elections are set to occur later this year after the president assumes office. The constitution, ratified in January 2014, restricts the presidency to two consecutive four-year terms.Currently, Mohammed Morsi faces trial on charges including inciting the murder of anti-government protesters, killing prison officers during a 2011 jailbreak, espionage, and conspiracy to commit terrorist acts.As for the candidates' platforms, Mr. Sisi has unveiled an ambitious agenda aimed at advancing agriculture, housing, education, and employment, particularly in underprivileged areas. However, he remains vague about funding, apart from urging collective effort and reduced profit margins for both state and private enterprises. His campaign slogan, Long live Egypt! underscores his assertion that a victory would signify the political demise of the Muslim Brotherhood. Mr. Sisi garners support from prominent business figures and a wide spectrum of political parties, ranging from the Islamist right to the moderate left.Hamdeen Sabahi, a prominent leftist since the 1970s, appeals to younger voters who prefer a civilian leader over a military one. His campaign, under the banner We will pursue our dream, pledges to tackle corruption and inefficiency while advocating for civil rights. Like Sisi, Sabahi opposes re-legalizing Morsi's Muslim Brotherhood, which is outlawed as a terrorist organization. His support base primarily consists of left-wing parties and movements.The election's fairness is in question due to ongoing security and political instability. The Muslim Brotherhood continues protests against Morsi's ousting, met with a violent crackdown by authorities, resulting in hundreds of deaths and numerous arrests, fueling further unrest. Moreover, the mainstream media's overwhelming support for Mr. Sisi, coupled with the ban on the Brotherhood's media outlets in Egypt, limits opposition voices to less influential online platforms abroad.International monitoring of the election is limited. The US-based Carter Center has opted out, though the European Union plans to observe the vote nationwide. The Arab League will deploy 100 monitors, and the African Union will send a mission despite Egypt's suspension from the organization last year.A call for a boycott has emerged from several Islamist parties, although some have endorsed Sisi. The Muslim Brotherhood, viewing Morsi as the legitimate president, rejects the election. The pro-Morsi National Alliance to Support Legitimacy labels the vote a farce, and the Salafist Front deems it illegitimate. The Building and Development Party, linked to the Gamaa Islamiya, reports most members favor a boycott. Additionally, the secular 6 April Youth Movement, key in the uprising against Hosni Mubarak, also advocates for a boycott, criticizing the election as a means to enthrone Sisi.The incoming president will face significant domestic challenges, including political, economic, security, and social issues. Public expectations include addressing unemployment, inequality, and corruption, with restoring security being a paramount concern. Internationally, the new leader must navigate maintaining strong ties with the US and Western nations while mending relations with countries that backed Morsi, such as Turkey, Qatar, and to some extent, Iran.BBC Monitoring provides insights and analysis from global TV, radio, web, and print media. For more information, follow BBC Monitoring on Twitter and Facebook.

text: The centuries-old tradition of church bell-ringing is under threat because of a shortage of new recruits. A recent BBC local radio survey reveals the growing challenge of enticing newcomers to the ancient art of bell-ringing. At the annual Central Council of Church Bell Ringers conference, three-quarters of attendees reported that attracting new members has become increasingly difficult over the past decade. Particularly concerning is the struggle to engage the younger generation, with nearly 80% of delegates indicating that recruiting individuals under 21 is a significant hurdle.Dickon Love, tower captain at St James Garlickhythe in London, challenges the stereotype that bell-ringing is a pastime for elderly, bearded men akin to Morris dancing. Bell-ringing is exciting for the mind, he asserts. It's the best form of heavy metal; it's a big loud noise, it keeps you fit, there's a competitive element as well. And it's a very social thing to do - after each practice without fail you can find us down the local pub.Despite these challenges, St James Garlickhythe has successfully attracted new members. They boast a fresh set of eight bells, installed four years ago, and a newly-formed band of ringers, including a professor of astrophysics and the art director of a renowned magazine.Pete McCoy, tower captain at St Mary's Church in Walkley, Sheffield, who met his wife Judith through bell-ringing, notes that today's teenagers face more distractions than in his youth. There weren't so many things for a teenager or young person to do as there are today, he reflects. And is it cool to ring bells? I think it is. But does everyone else?In the UK, there are nearly 40,000 bell-ringers, yet just over half of the 180 delegates surveyed at the Portsmouth conference in May believe that declining church attendance is a key factor in recruitment difficulties. According to the survey, 54% agree while 43% disagree.Kate Flavell from the Central Council of Church Bell Ringers emphasizes the need for the 66 affiliated societies to enhance their promotional efforts. In collaboration with the Heritage Open Days initiative, they plan to showcase bell-ringing to the public at 500 locations, including St Peter Mancroft in Norwich, where the first full peal was performed in May 1715.

text: UK Chancellor George Osborne is to embark on a week-long visit to China to boost commercial and political ties with the country. He reiterated the trip's goal of discovering new market opportunities to benefit both nations.The highlight of Osborne's visit will be the UK-China Economic and Financial Dialogue in Beijing. Joining him are Treasury Minister Lord O'Neill, Business Secretary Sajid Javid, and Energy Secretary Amber Rudd. Liu also held talks with the prime minister, David Cameron, and the foreign secretary, Philip Hammond, with the aim of strengthening relations between the two countries. This visit marks a further thaw in relations between the two countries after the controversy in 2012 over the meeting between David Cameron and the Dalai Lama. The highlight of Osborne’s visit will be the UK-China economic and financial dialogue in Beijing, to which he will be accompanied by the minister of the treasury, Lord O’Neil, the minister for business, Sajid Javid, and the minister for energy, Amber Rudd. He restates his intention to find new markets for both countries. Osborne and Cameron both visited China last year, and the United Kingdom has now joined the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, backed by China. Growth has been recently revised down from 7.4 per cent to 7.3 per cent in China, which is its lowest rate for almost twenty-five years. The government’s goal for this year is a growth rate of about seven per cent. In recent days the slowdown in this giant of the economic world has caused considerable declines in all the financial markets.

text: David Cameron has visited a Lebanese refugee camp amid the crisis triggered by war in neighbouring Syria. Prime Minister David Cameron embarked on his inaugural visit to Lebanon, where he met with a family in a refugee camp in the Bekaa Valley, who are set to be relocated to the UK. I wanted to come here to see for myself and to hear for myself stories of refugees, Cameron stated, emphasizing the importance of firsthand experience. Earlier this month, Cameron informed MPs that the UK plans to accept up to 20,000 Syrian refugees over the next five years. To facilitate this process, he appointed Richard Harrington as minister for Syrian refugees, ensuring that those arriving in the UK receive a warm welcome.Cameron's visit coincides with a significant meeting of European Union interior ministers in Brussels, where discussions are underway regarding the redistribution of 160,000 asylum seekers across 23 EU states through mandatory quotas. Home Secretary Theresa May is expected to attend, opposing the EU-wide quota system for refugees. Under EU law, the UK, Ireland, and Denmark are exempt from this quota plan.BBC deputy political editor James Landale reports that Cameron's visit to Lebanon aims to counter criticism that Britain is not sufficiently addressing Europe's refugee crisis. Cameron toured a refugee camp in the Bekaa Valley, just a mile from the Syrian border, to meet families supported by British aid. He also visited a Beirut school, funded by UK aid, where Syrian and Lebanese children study together. Cameron argues that providing aid to refugees in Lebanon, Turkey, Jordan, and Syria is more effective than encouraging perilous journeys to Europe. He claims that British aid is preventing hundreds of thousands of refugees from heading to Europe, although aid agencies suggest that poverty and the inability to pay traffickers play a larger role. While welcoming British aid, they argue it falls short of what's needed. Cameron's visit aims to reshape a contentious debate that has not always favored him.Cameron expressed his focus on helping Syrian refugees in Lebanon and Jordan, discouraging dangerous journeys to Europe, and instead welcoming refugees from camps to the UK. After meeting with Lebanon's Prime Minister Tammam Salam, Cameron reaffirmed the UK's commitment to bolstering Lebanon's security. He noted that over 5,000 Lebanese soldiers have been trained, and the UK has assisted in constructing watchtowers along the Syrian border. The UK will also train, equip, and mentor the Lebanese armed forces, Cameron added.Lebanon is set to receive £29 million of the additional £100 million in UK aid for Syria and neighboring countries, announced by Cameron earlier this month. This aid will provide food packages, clean water, blankets, stoves, mattresses, counseling, and play areas for children. Lebanon hosts 1.1 million registered Syrian refugees, accounting for over a quarter of its population. The camp Cameron visited is one of 1,500 in the Bekaa Valley, operated by the UN's refugee agency.Cameron also attended the first day of the academic year at Sed el Bouchrieh school in Beirut, where Syrian and Lebanese children are integrated into classes, supported by UK aid. Former Labour foreign secretary David Miliband criticized the UK government for agreeing to resettle only 20,000 refugees over five years. As head of the International Rescue Committee (IRC), Miliband argued that accepting just 4,000 refugees annually from Syria is insufficient, equating it to the daily arrivals on the Greek island of Lesbos. Each country needs to shoulder the burden and agree to both relocate refugees who have reached the continent and resettle the most vulnerable from the Middle East, he stated.

text: More than a third of the workforce at a wind energy firm in Argyll and Bute have been told their jobs are under threat. CS Wind has notified employees that as many as 60 positions at its Machrihanish factory might be eliminated due to a shortage of orders. This announcement comes less than a year after the South Korean company took control of the site, located on the former RAF airbase. The potential impact on plans to construct a new facility dedicated to offshore wind equipment remains uncertain. CS Wind has not yet provided any comments on the situation.The company acquired Wind Towers Scotland (WTS) last April, pledging to generate new employment opportunities at the rural location near Campbeltown. Currently, the firm employs approximately 150 people. Local councillor Rory Colville expressed his understanding that the new factory project for offshore wind equipment is still on track, with construction anticipated to commence in July. He stated, There's no indication that has been put off. The firm is seeking assurances from the governments at Holyrood and Westminster that they are still committed to wind energy. It's really important for the local economy that we keep CS Wind going.Mr. Colville noted that investments have been made in deep-water facilities to support the wind energy sector and advocated for the former airbase to receive Enterprise Zone status. The site was sold to a community-led consortium for £1 in 2012 and is among six locations vying to become the UK's first spaceport.Scottish Energy Minister Paul Wheelhouse acknowledged the challenging market conditions for onshore wind energy companies and criticized UK ministers for their failure to establish a viable 'route to market' for new projects. He remarked, The announcement is disappointing news for the workforce at Machrihanish and the wider Campbeltown community and will be an extremely difficult time for those affected and their families. I understand from my own discussions with management that this is part of CS Wind UK's drive to improve the long-term sustainability of the Machrihanish facility in the face of challenging market conditions.Argyll and Bute MSP Michael Russell mentioned that he has communicated with both the company and the energy minister regarding the threat to jobs. He commented, I have been seeking assurances on the future of the staff who have been put on notice about possible job losses.

text: Russia will not compete at next month’s Paralympics in Rio after losing an appeal against a ban imposed for state-sponsored doping. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the International Paralympic Committee's (IPC) decision to ban all Russian athletes from competing, following allegations of a state-sponsored doping scheme detailed in the McLaren report. Russian Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev criticized the ruling as cynical, accusing certain Paralympic leaders of attempting to squeeze out strong competitors. He lamented the decision as a blow to all people with disabilities, not just Russians.The CAS panel, which intends to publish the full rationale for its decision later, stated that the IPC's blanket ban on the Russian team was proportionate in the circumstances. It noted that the Russian Paralympic Committee failed to provide evidence to counter the IPC's claims. The Paralympic Games are set to begin on September 7.In contrast, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) did not impose a blanket ban on Russian athletes for the Olympic Games, a decision that drew criticism for disregarding the World Anti-Doping Agency's (WADA) recommendation. Instead, the IOC allowed individual sports federations to decide on Russian participation, with a three-person IOC panel making the final call. Ultimately, over 270 Russian athletes competed, securing 56 medals and placing fourth in the medal tally.Russia initially planned to send 267 athletes across 18 sports to the Paralympics. The CAS statement clarified that it did not consider the natural justice rights or personality rights of individual Russian athletes. Russia's Paralympic team's lawyer, Alexei Karpenko, acknowledged the decision as final, revealing plans to appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, a process expected to take one to two years. So I'm afraid Russian Paralympians will not be going to the Games in any case, Karpenko remarked.Sir Philip Craven, IPC president, expressed satisfaction with the CAS ruling, despite describing Russia's anti-doping system as broken, corrupted and entirely compromised. He emphasized, This is not a day for celebration, expressing sympathy for the Russian athletes who will miss out. It is a sad day for the Paralympic movement, but we hope it marks a new beginning, Craven stated, hoping the decision would spark change in Russia and allow the Russian Paralympic Committee to return, ensuring fair competition.Russian sports minister Vitaly Mutko condemned the ban as political and outside the legal framework, while lawyer Karpenko described it as a black day for the sports judiciary. He expressed deep disappointment, arguing that the rights of Russian Paralympians were blatantly violated. Regardless of the Russian Paralympics Committee's guilt, punishing innocent athletes without a chance to defend themselves—an opportunity given to Russian Olympic athletes—is a flagrant violation of human rights.Dmitry Svishchev, head of Russia's parliamentary sports committee, labeled the CAS decision an inhumane act. Speaking to Tass news agency, he criticized the court's unprecedented impudence and lack of principle, questioning how athletes who earned their place through courage could be barred. Whatever this court is called, it is an inhumane court, Svishchev declared, advocating respect for athletes who overcome hardships.The McLaren report, led by Canadian law professor Richard McLaren, revealed Russia's sports ministry manipulated athletes' urine samples from 2011 to 2015, involving 27 samples across eight Para-sports, five of which are summer sports under IPC governance. The IPC uncovered evidence of sample swapping during the Sochi 2014 Paralympic Games and plans to reanalyze all Russian samples from the event.Oksana Savchenko, an eight-time Russian Paralympic champion, expressed shock at the decision, noting, Yesterday evening the mood seemed positive. Everyone thought our guys would finally go. Roman Petushkov, a six-time champion, echoed this sentiment, describing the ruling as inhumane treatment and humiliation.Karen Pickering, a four-time British Olympic athlete and world champion, praised the IPC's firm stance, stating, Cas did the right thing by upholding it. She criticized the IOC's inaction, asserting, If a country cheats, you sanction them. That means Russia should not have been competing in Rio.Despite the ban, the Paralympics will proceed as planned, though facing significant budget cuts due to Brazil's economic struggles and poor ticket sales. These cuts will impact venues, workforce, and transport. Delayed travel grants will now be issued to athletes, but 10 countries may still face challenges in sending teams to Rio.

text: You would think securing promotion to the top flight of a national league would mean a lucrative bonus for any footballer. Despite clinching promotion to the Welsh Premier League, the players of Cardiff Metropolitan University's football team haven't earned a single penny. Instead, these student-athletes, who triumphed in the Welsh League Division One, must pay to play. Each season, they pay us a £150 subscription, which funds our football budget for the year, explained Dr. Christian Edwards, director of football and former Wales international.Edwards emphasized that academics come first. They're at the university primarily to study and must excel academically to earn their degrees before focusing on football and social life, he noted. Many players have been with the team for five or six years, making significant sacrifices. Charlie Corsby, for instance, is a PhD student, and we have several pursuing Masters. They're growing both as athletes and scholars.The university's football journey began when Cardiff Metropolitan University, formerly UWIC, merged with Inter Cardiff, a founding member of the League of Wales, in 2000. Last season, the team narrowly missed promotion, losing to Haverfordwest County on the final day. This setback fueled their determination, culminating in a decisive 3-0 victory over Taffs Well to secure their place.We set our sights on promotion from the start, Edwards told BBC Wales Sport. Barry Town and Goytre were tough competitors, but we're thrilled to have come out on top. Promotion required more than just on-field success; the university also invested in infrastructure to meet FAW domestic licence requirements.Facing the challenges of Welsh football's top tier, Edwards remains optimistic. We've played Welsh Premier League teams in the Welsh Cup and held our own, he said. While we don't expect to dominate, we believe we can compete. Our six-year journey is ongoing, and we see it as progress rather than an endpoint.Born in Caerphilly, Edwards began his career at Swansea City and earned a cap for Wales against Switzerland in 1996, substituting for current national team manager Chris Coleman. His career also included stints with Nottingham Forest and Bristol Rovers before retiring at 30. Edwards later spent four seasons with Aberystwyth Town in the Welsh Premier League, including a spell as caretaker manager in 2009.Since 2010, Edwards has been part of Cardiff Metropolitan University's School of Sport, balancing his roles as lecturer and director of football with his academic pursuits. Retiring in 2006 led me back to academia, he said. My wife joked I couldn't just do DIY, and I always loved studying. If not a footballer, I might have been a PE teacher.This year, Edwards celebrated another achievement: earning a doctorate from the university in January. Originally, I planned a three-year degree and a PGCE, but opportunities for a Masters and then a PhD arose, he shared. I never aimed for a Doctorate, but my thesis on the football club's culture owes much to the team and coaching staff.

text: Generally speaking, England will be very happy to have won the Test series against Sri Lanka without really breaking sweat. England's nine-wicket victory in the second Test at Chester-le-Street might not have matched the rapid finish of the first Test, but it was nonetheless a decisive win. Sri Lanka struggled to compete throughout the series. England's coach, Trevor Bayliss, rated their performance an eight out of ten. Personally, I'd give them a seven. As captain Alastair Cook acknowledged, there were moments when they eased off, though this may be nitpicking considering their dominance.Assessing a team's performance is challenging when faced with weaker opposition, as Sri Lanka has been. However, one undeniable highlight is James Anderson's exceptional bowling. Even against elite batsmen, Anderson's skill would remain evident. His ascent to the top of the Test bowling rankings is well-earned. Fast bowling is unpredictable, heavily dependent on rhythm, which Anderson lacked in South Africa. Now, he's back in form, effortlessly taking wickets and troubling batsmen worldwide with his ability to move the ball both ways.Anderson's early-season stint with Lancashire, where he claimed 12 wickets at an average of 20.75 in three matches, was crucial. No matter how experienced, regaining rhythm can't be achieved solely in practice nets.In stark contrast, Steven Finn, who excelled in South Africa, appears to have lost his rhythm. Despite putting in the same effort, the ball lacks its usual snap. He has limited chances to regain form before the final Test at Lord's on June 9, with only one potential T20 Blast match for Middlesex.Finn should play at Lord's. Although there's talk of giving Jake Ball a chance, Finn's familiarity with the ground could help him rediscover his form. Even in victory, teams must evolve, and England's management has areas of concern.Jonny Bairstow has shone with the bat but remains a work in progress as a wicketkeeper. While his position isn't immediately threatened, repeated mistakes could draw scrutiny. Slow-motion replays can be unforgiving, but errors happen in the blink of an eye.Another concern is Nick Compton's form at number three. Despite his relief at scoring 22 not out in Durham, he hasn't produced significant runs for England or Middlesex this summer. Lord's, a venue he knows well, offers a chance for redemption on a flatter pitch. Winning the toss and batting first would provide him a prime opportunity to secure his place.Compton's future with England doesn't solely depend on his performance in the third Test. With a break before facing Pakistan on July 14, he could regain form with Middlesex. However, failure to score will increase scrutiny.Alastair Cook's position, however, is secure. Becoming the first Englishman to reach 10,000 Test runs is a monumental achievement. Cook has done it the hard way—opening the batting, managing captaincy pressures, and often facing uncertainty about his partner. His determination and focus are commendable.Cook's style might not draw crowds, but his ability to anchor innings is invaluable. His captaincy, once as steadfast as his batting, has evolved over the past year, boosting his confidence. Yet, he remains able to focus solely on batting when needed, a testament to his mental strength.Cook's focus has been a defining trait since his debut in Nagpur, where he impressed with scores of 60 and a century after a long journey from the West Indies. His ability to concentrate on batting is remarkable, and long may he continue to do so.Jonathan Agnew shared these insights with BBC Sport's James Gheerbrant.

text: Reading moved in to the second round of the EFL Cup thanks to Liam Kelly's well-taken brace against Gillingham. The Royals managed to break the deadlock in the 71st minute, thanks to a brilliant strike from 21-year-old Liam Kelly at the edge of the area. He later sealed the victory by scoring from close range, capitalizing on excellent setup play by former Swansea winger Modou Barrow. Earlier in the match, Reading's goalkeeper Anssi Jaakkola made a crucial save to prevent Tom Eaves from converting what was arguably Gillingham's best opportunity.The match concluded with a final score of Reading 2, Gillingham 0. In the second half, Stephen Quinn of Reading missed a chance when his left-footed shot from the center of the box went high and wide. A corner was conceded by Max Ehmer, leading to another missed attempt by Gillingham's Josh Parker, whose long-range right-footed shot veered high and wide.Liam Kelly's first goal came from a right-footed shot outside the box, finding the bottom left corner after being assisted by Modou Barrow. Pelle Clement of Reading had a left-footed effort from the right side of the box that narrowly missed the target. The match saw a delay due to an injury to Gillingham's Luke O'Neill.Conor Wilkinson of Gillingham committed a foul, allowing Sam Smith of Reading to win a free kick in the attacking half. Substitutions followed, with Gillingham's Ben Chapman replacing Jake Hessenthaler and Liam Nash coming on for Tom Eaves. Reading's Stephen Quinn replaced Josh Barrett, and Axel Óskar Andresson came in for an injured Omar Richards.Gillingham's Scott Wagstaff earned a free kick on the left wing, while Reading's Liam Moore had a header saved from the center of the box. A corner was conceded by Jake Hessenthaler, and another attempt by Liam Kelly from outside the box went slightly high. Tom Eaves had a right-footed shot saved in the bottom right corner, resulting in a corner conceded by Anssi Jaakkola.Throughout the match, various fouls were committed, including those by Reading's Chris Gunter and Omar Richards, and Gillingham's Tom Eaves. Modou Barrow's left-footed shot from outside the box was narrowly high, and Darren Oldaker of Gillingham secured a free kick in the defensive half.In the end, Reading's solid performance, highlighted by Kelly's decisive goals and Jaakkola's key saves, ensured their 2-0 victory over Gillingham.

text: After months of secrecy, the sequel to the late Stieg Larsson's best-selling Millennium series has been published. David Lagercrantz's novel, *The Girl in the Spider's Web*, picks up the tale of the iconic punk hacker Lisbeth Salander, a character originally brought to life in Stieg Larsson's *The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo*. Lagercrantz faced the daunting task of staying true to Larsson's beloved characters while navigating criticism from Larsson's long-time partner.There's been so much secrecy about this book, so I'm longing to see what people think, Lagercrantz told the BBC days before the global release of *The Girl in the Spider's Web*. More than 80 million copies of Larsson's Millennium Trilogy have been sold, adding to Lagercrantz's pre-publication anxiety.I've felt pressure from the start, he confessed. I'm absolutely terrified. But I think the pressure actually made me a better writer. It would be a disgrace if I didn't live up to [Stieg Larsson's] books or at least try my best.Larsson, who passed away at 50 in 2004 from a heart attack, never witnessed the phenomenal success of his novels, which were adapted into three Swedish films and an American remake starring Rooney Mara and Daniel Craig. Despite a 32-year relationship, Larsson's partner, Eva Gabrielsson, received nothing from his estate under Swedish law, leading to a prolonged legal dispute with Larsson's father and brother, the estate's heirs.In December 2013, Lagercrantz was commissioned by Larsson's estate and Swedish publisher Norstedts to continue the adventures of Lisbeth Salander and journalist Mikael Blomkvist. However, Gabrielsson criticized the choice, labeling it a money-making stunt that would have appalled Larsson.Lagercrantz admitted the criticism was challenging. It was tough, he said. All I wanted to do was to follow my passion and tell a good story. This has been the thrill of my life. The only thing that troubles me and makes me sad is that Eva Gabrielsson and the family haven't reached a settlement about the book. She could call me anything, I just have the deepest sympathy for her.Despite the tension, Lagercrantz remains hopeful for reconciliation. No, he replied when asked if there's been contact with Gabrielsson. She's very angry and I accept that. I'm daydreaming that we will one day have a good conversation about it. She called me an idiotic choice—well, the readers have to decide. She said I'm not like Stieg Larsson, and I accept that. But if you want a copycat the circle would be so narrow.Born in 1962, Lagercrantz, son of Swedish author and critic Olof Lagercrantz, began his career as a journalist for Expressen before debuting as an author in 1997 with *Ultimate High*, chronicling Goran Kropp's Everest climb without oxygen or sherpas. His other works include *Fall of Man in Wilmslow*, a novel about codebreaker Alan Turing, and the autobiography *I am Zlatan Ibrahimovic*, which he ghostwrote for the Swedish football star.Fascinated by unconventional geniuses, Lagercrantz was drawn to Salander, who even invaded his dreams during the writing process. I was absolutely obsessed. I was quite terrible to live with. My wife and kids were very kind. I was scared I would do her an injustice. In the beginning I thought it would be easy to write her. She is such an extreme character. Many people are scared of Lisbeth Salander and so was I. I asked myself all the time: am I worthy?The project was shrouded in secrecy; Lagercrantz wrote on a computer without internet access, avoiding digital communication. Final proofs were hand-delivered by couriers. We used code-words and we didn't email anything, he recalled. We met in the cellars and things like that. The plot was influenced by the National Security Agency and the [Edward] Snowden affair. I was living in the same reality I was writing about. We were quite paranoid all the time. I'm a talkative guy so it was hard, but I kept the secrets. There were no leaks, it was extraordinary.In Sweden, the book's title is *Det som inte dödar oss* (What Doesn't Kill Us). As for continuing the Millennium series, Lagercrantz remains uncertain. That we will see. The only thing I know is that I found myself as a writer. Offers from around the globe are under discussion with his agent. One thing is for certain—I won't be Stieg Larsson for the whole of my life. I want to write new books. It's good to be insecure.*The Girl in the Spider's Web*, published by Quercus in the UK, is now available.

text: David Cameron's hurried visit to Paris on Monday night is yet another significant sign that his EU reforms - dismissed as weak by critics in the UK - are seen by some in the EU as going too far. France is expressing concern over the UK Prime Minister's efforts to shield non-euro nations from eurozone regulations. While this may appear reasonable—since most EU countries utilize the euro—France suspects ulterior motives behind the actions of David Cameron and UK Chancellor George Osborne. The French government fears this move aims to secure an unfair advantage for London's financial hub and potentially grant the UK a backdoor veto on eurozone and broader EU financial legislation.Facing a sluggish economy, French President François Hollande, who is poised to enter the re-election race, is wary of any scenario where Britain gains financially while France's hands are tied by eurozone constraints. Just two weeks ago, as David Cameron's draft reform plans were about to be unveiled in Brussels, French officials, concerned about the language regarding non-eurozone safeguards, delayed the publication for several hours.For Cameron's reforms to proceed, all EU leaders must agree to them at the upcoming summit on Thursday. However, France could challenge, debate, or even block the Prime Minister's aspirations for a deal. A likely outcome is that after prolonged discussions behind closed doors, the summit may conclude with a compromise that critics often deride as typical EU ambiguity.In classic EU fashion, each party hopes to claim a victory. France might boast that Britain failed to secure a veto over eurozone legislation, a point Cameron never pursued. Meanwhile, central and eastern European nations secured Britain's commitment to strengthen NATO's presence in eastern Europe as a pre-summit incentive. text: I have been working now for more than two decades and I've not seen a measles epidemic of this severity, says Doctor Raza Hasan, as he shows me around the measles isolation ward of the Lahore Children's Hospital. The pediatric ward is overcrowded, with babies and young children sharing beds. At one point, the hospital was inundated with up to 70 new patients daily. Many of these children are covered in rashes and suffering from high fevers, some clinging to life. In a corner, a boy lies still, eyes rolled back, as flies crawl on his face.Since the measles epidemic spread from southern Pakistan to Lahore and other areas of Punjab province earlier this year, at least 40 children have died in this hospital. The crisis is a heavy burden for Dr. Hasan, who recounts incidents where grieving families have attacked hospital staff upon learning of their children's deaths.Although measles is rarely fatal, it can lead to severe complications such as meningitis and pneumonia, especially in developing countries where malnutrition weakens children's immune systems. Some of them are arriving very late at the hospital, Dr. Hasan explains. Their parents don't take them to doctors or get any treatment after complications develop at home, so when they come here, there is not much we can do. Some are in the final stage of life or already dead with meningitis or pneumonia.However, this doesn't fully explain why so many children in Pakistan are contracting measles. The epidemic has spread swiftly, with thousands of cases reported nationwide and 239 deaths between January and April 2013, as per Pakistan's national measles coordinator.Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, director-general of health services for Punjab province, attributes this to low vaccination coverage. In some districts, there are even pockets with no vaccination coverage. The average for Punjab is 58%, he states.In Lahore, we visit the modest home of Nasara and Mohammed Ashfaq. Despite scorching temperatures exceeding 40°C, their home lacks fans. Mohammed cradles his daughter Yasmeen, who is covered in a measles rash and has a dangerously high fever. Just days ago, their nine-month-old son Ehsan succumbed to measles complications at Lahore Children's Hospital. Fearing for Yasmeen, the family hesitates to take her to the hospital, hoping for her recovery at home. Like her brother, Yasmeen was not properly vaccinated.I didn't get him vaccinated because I was on my own at home with so many children, Nasara confesses. Going out for vaccinations was difficult because they were small.Doctors urge families to ensure their children are vaccinated but acknowledge that official vaccination programs have often been mismanaged, resulting in many missing out. We have removed nine district managers for poor program performance, says Dr. Tanvir Ahmed. We've improved our monitoring and supervision.In response, an emergency measles vaccination campaign recently covered 2.6 million children in Lahore. Another 11 million children are set to be inoculated across Punjab in June. Health experts are optimistic that the epidemic will be under control in the province by mid-July, with sufficient vaccine stocks available.However, the situation is different in the southern province of Sindh, where the outbreak began. Mass vaccination programs there are not expected to start until autumn, potentially worsening the epidemic in the region, which already has the highest number of cases in the country.

text: Labour remains committed to renewing the Trident nuclear weapons system, new shadow defence secretary Nia Griffith has said. In a recent interview with Forces TV, Ms. Griffith revealed that she had once harbored serious doubts about Trident, but emphasized that Labour's stance remains supportive of it, and this is unlikely to change. Ms. Griffith took over from Clive Lewis after Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn reshuffled his shadow cabinet earlier this month. Mr. Lewis's speech at the conference regarding Trident underwent last-minute changes, as it was believed that the leader's office prevented him from firmly committing to renewing the UK's nuclear weapons system. Although Labour's official policy supports the renewal of Trident, Jeremy Corbyn, a known CND advocate, aims to shift the party's stance and has initiated a defense review to scrutinize the matter.During her interview, Ms. Griffith reiterated that Labour delegates at the September party conference endorsed the weapons system, stating, and that is a commitment that we will stick to. She stressed that Labour must not vacillate on Trident but acknowledged the necessity for the UK to advocate for multilateral disarmament. What we do need to do now, and there is a very strong mood for this, both within the Labour Party and in the broader public, is really push forward on the multilateral nuclear disarmament, on the multilateral approach of bringing people together across the globe to try to make our world a safer place, she remarked.The renewal of Trident involves producing four replacement submarines, with current estimates placing the cost at £31 billion. The contentious issue of nuclear arms renewal sparked division within Labour during a vote in July, where 140 Labour MPs supported renewal, 47 opposed it, and the rest abstained.The Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (CND), advocating for a global ban on nuclear weapons, expressed disappointment over Ms. Griffith's remarks, suggesting the issue was being sidelined. CND General Secretary Kate Hudson stated, Labour hasn't debated Trident for 20 years but it insists on clinging to its old policy in spite of the fact that the majority of Labour members oppose Trident and the party leader has been elected twice with a strong anti-Trident position. She urged Labour members to ensure the defense review is published, accompanied by a comprehensive democratic debate within the party and at its next conference.In parallel developments, Mr. Corbyn has expanded his team by appointing seven new shadow ministers, bringing the total to 68 frontbenchers. The newly appointed shadow ministers include Paula Sherriff (women and equalities), Richard Burden (transport), Wayne David (defence), Khalid Mahmood (foreign office), Rupa Huq (home affairs), Lyn Brown (home affairs), and Gill Furniss (business).Additionally, Dame Rosie Winterton, the former chief whip, has been appointed as the party's envoy responsible for relations with Labour's international sister parties on the Party of European Socialists. Her removal as chief whip, part of the reshuffle following Mr. Corbyn's re-election, had caused discontent among many Labour MPs.

text: China's Communist Party and its more than two-million-man army aren't supposed to like video games. In the year 2000, China officially banned home-video consoles, which had been gaining popularity throughout the 1990s, due to concerns that they were corrupting the nation's youth. This move was reminiscent of King Canute's attempt to hold back the tide, as the government sought to resist the surge of capitalism and Western cultural products. Ultimately, the effort was unsuccessful, as consumer demand drowned out warnings about electronic heroin. Consoles found their way into the grey market, and the gaming industry transitioned online.Today, the gaming industry in China is booming, valued at over 50 billion RMB ($7.9 billion; £5.2 billion) annually. The Communist Party and its military have now embraced this sector. A recent example is Glorious Mission, a video game initially developed by the Chinese military for training purposes. Since its public release a few months ago, it has been downloaded over a million times. Although it resembles a typical shoot 'em up game, it serves as China's latest propaganda tool.Designed as a training aid, Glorious Mission features Chinese soldiers controlling virtual People's Liberation Army troops in various battlefield scenarios. State-run television has broadcast images of soldiers engaging with the game. Notably, the virtual adversaries often bear a resemblance to the US and its allies, prompting questions about the real-life scenarios being simulated. The game's public release aims to instill patriotic and military core values, according to army sources.Gu Kai, vice-president of Giant Network Technology, the game's developer, believes the game could inspire new army recruits. I would hope that somebody will play the game and fulfill their dream, he says. Most young boys, from the bottom of their hearts, want to be a soldier. They like to fight, they like to win, and if this video game can make that dream come true, I won't be surprised.The propaganda within the game is sometimes overt. One stage of the game reportedly captures the fiery atmosphere of camp life. In a Shanghai internet café, nearly all of the 100 terminals are occupied by gamers engrossed in combat with various enemies, from goblins to aliens to humans. One young man, who spends over 10 hours a week gaming there, acknowledges the potential influence of such games. It's possible, he says. Most of the players here are young. A military video game could make you feel familiar with and then develop an affinity for the army.Glorious Mission signifies a significant shift in the Chinese military's approach. Beyond censoring the internet and controlling online discourse, China is now leveraging digital platforms to its advantage. The country already employs an army of Communist Party bloggers to support the government. The gaming industry, once shunned, is now a strategic tool.Recent state media reports suggest that China may soon officially lift its longstanding ban on consoles, reflecting a broader acceptance of the gaming industry. Gu Kai notes that officials have stopped worrying about video games. Most of them are promoting gaming as a new, hopeful, and fast-growing industry. At least here in Shanghai, all the officials are very open and supportive.China is not the first to use video games for military training; Glorious Mission shares similarities with a game developed a decade ago for the US military, both as a training tool and recruitment lure. However, China's ambition to influence public sentiment and foster nationalism through gaming is a more complex endeavor. In China's virtual landscape, this battle for hearts and minds is poised to escalate.

text: Christian Eriksen scored twice as Tottenham proved far too strong for spirited Hull City at White Hart Lane. In a commanding performance, Denmark's Christian Eriksen found the net twice, propelling Tottenham Hotspur to a solid 3-0 victory over Hull City, further cementing their fifth-place position in the Premier League with their eighth win of the season. The initial breakthrough came swiftly, as Danny Rose, after a skillful play down the left, set up Eriksen to score within the first 15 minutes. The second half saw Kyle Walker mirror Rose's efforts from the right, extinguishing any Hull hopes of a comeback.Eriksen narrowly missed a hat-trick when his exquisite free-kick was deflected onto the post by Hull's goalkeeper, David Marshall. Victor Wanyama capitalized on the rebound, sealing the third goal from close range. Despite the lopsided scoreline, Hull City matched their hosts during significant stretches, though they could not argue with the defeat. Their defensive woes continued, having conceded 35 goals in 16 matches and equaling a club record with their sixth consecutive away loss.Tottenham dominated possession, firing 27 shots in total, though clear chances were scarce. The wing-backs, Rose and Walker, were instrumental, creating the most opportunities. Rose's speedy advance down the flank, assisted by Jan Vertonghen's long ball, set up Eriksen's first goal, a powerful strike into the net. Spurs' three-man defense, featuring Eric Dier alongside Vertonghen and Toby Alderweireld, allowed the wing-backs more freedom to attack, leading to their second goal. Dier's lofted pass found Walker, who delivered a low cross for Eriksen to finish at the back post, marking his fifth goal in four league games.Rose's contribution continued as he won the free-kick that led to Spurs' third goal, concluding a standout performance. Despite the disparity in resources and league standings, Hull displayed resilience, managing 10 shots against a top-five side—a feat they struggled to achieve against lesser teams. With more composure, they might have leveled the score at 1-1.Jake Livermore, facing his former team, was Hull's standout player and nearly equalized. His first chance came amidst Hull's pressure after falling behind, but Hugo Lloris denied him. Another opportunity arose as Spurs fans grew restless, but Livermore's efforts were thwarted by Lloris once more. Just minutes later, Eriksen secured his second goal, effectively ending Hull's challenge.Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino remarked, I think it was a game we dominated. The most important is the three points, to be close to the top four. On Eriksen, he commented, He was very close to a hat-trick. It was a very good performance for him. Addressing rumors about Eric Dier, Pochettino assured, He's 100% our player. He's very important for us.Hull's manager, Mike Phelan, praised his team's attitude despite the defeat, saying, They've come here and played the ball, controlled it... but we're on the end of a 3-0 defeat. We have to stay positive. He expressed hope for improvement and potential additions to the squad in January.Tottenham will host Burnley at White Hart Lane on Sunday at 16:00 GMT, while Hull returns to London to face West Ham on Saturday at 15:00 GMT. The match concluded with Tottenham Hotspur decisively defeating Hull City 3-0, a result that underscored their dominance and Hull's ongoing struggles.

text: The Football League season is poised for another dramatic climax as six teams aim to be promoted by winning their respective play-off finals at Wembley. The stakes are high this weekend as Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday face off in a Championship showdown on Saturday, a match with a staggering £170 million prize for the victor. Meanwhile, Barnsley and Millwall will battle for the League One title on Sunday, with AFC Wimbledon and Plymouth Argyle concluding the 2015-16 season in the League Two final on Monday.Hull City manager Steve Bruce, no stranger to promotion battles, having led Birmingham City to the Premier League in 2002 and 2007 and Hull in 2013, is about to make his debut at Wembley for a play-off final. This season has been a rollercoaster for Hull, marred by inconsistency and nearly losing a 3-0 advantage in their semi-final against Derby County. Bruce remarked on BBC Radio Humberside, You can just detect there's a big game around the corner. The players are tackling each other and champing at the bit. You just have to put them on a little bit of a leash at times because we need to let them go on Saturday. Hull's last Wembley appearance was in 2014, where they faced defeat in the FA Cup final against Arsenal. Bruce's extensive managerial experience could be pivotal in their quest to return to the Premier League.In contrast, Sheffield Wednesday's head coach Carlos Carvalhal is experiencing Wembley for the first time, having only watched English league football on TV as a child in Portugal. Carvalhal, who joined Wednesday in June 2015 after managing in Portugal and Turkey, guided his team to a strong finish this season. Their decisive play-off victories over Brighton secured their Wembley spot. Sheffield Wednesday has not graced the national stadium since 1993 and has only twice finished in the Championship's top half since their 2000 relegation. Carvalhal told BBC Radio Sheffield, Hull City are a strong team with a very spirited coach - they are a premier team and it will be very tough. My players know exactly what they need to do and we will prepare for this game like any of the others. We expect a very good answer from the players to the plan we will put into place.Barnsley, facing Millwall on Sunday, were in dire straits last November, languishing at the bottom of League One. However, under caretaker manager Paul Heckingbottom, they have turned their season around, winning the Johnstone's Paint Trophy and securing a play-off spot before thrashing Walsall 6-1 on aggregate in the semi-finals. Heckingbottom, who was part of Barnsley's 2006 play-off promotion, shared with BBC Radio Sheffield, Everything is bigger about the play-offs. It's not just the prize at the end, but the bigger opposition, better-quality football and away games at bigger stadiums that come in the Championship. It's a cup final after 46 rounds and a two-legged semi-final and that brings its own unique tension, adrenaline and excitement for everyone. That's what makes a win that much more sweeter.Millwall, seeking a swift return to the Championship after last season's relegation, have been revitalized under club legend Neil Harris. Harris, who orchestrated a squad overhaul, expressed pride in his team on BBC Radio London, We have come a long way as a group. We have a terrific bunch of lads and they have great spirit. Whatever happens on Sunday, the pride is back in the club and we have foundations to build on. Harris, Millwall's all-time top scorer, was part of the team that triumphed in the 2010 League One play-off final. He added, Barnsley played there this year but they didn't play against Millwall or in front of our fans there. The noise at The Den in the second leg against Bradford was something special. That is what we will have at Wembley, with 35,000 passionate fans going to back their team. Every time we have had that, the players have performed. You have to have the link between the terraces and the pitch at this club.On Monday, AFC Wimbledon stands on the brink of history, aiming to reach the third tier for the first time. Founded in 2002 after Wimbledon FC's controversial move to Milton Keynes, the club has climbed through five promotions to join the Football League in 2011. Under Neal Ardley's leadership since 2012, Wimbledon finished seventh after a strong end to the season. Ardley, a former Wimbledon midfielder, told BBC Radio London, Somebody asked me if it is the biggest game in the club's history. Terry Brown getting them into the Football League would have been, and maybe us staying in the Football League on the last day in 2013. But it is the biggest occasion in the club's history. Wimbledon and Wembley has a lovely ring to it and we know why. To take these fans to Wembley, it is a most unique club and a wonderful feeling for me and the players to do that for this group of fans - who, 14 years ago, were dealt the biggest kick you could possibly imagine and rolled their sleeves up and said 'no, it's not happening'.Plymouth Argyle, on the other hand, are returning to Wembley for the first time since 1996. The Devon club has experienced a tumultuous journey, from topping the Championship in 2004 to financial collapse seven years later. Relegation in 2010 led to administration and a drop to League Two in 2011, with players threatening to strike due to unpaid wages. Chris Webb, Argyle's president, told BBC Sport, We nearly died, so to be here in this position is absolutely fantastic. We had a torrid time with the players and staff not being paid for 10 months, but out of that we united the fans, the staff, and the city and the club was almost reborn. I believe if we can make that step at Wembley then we're well set up to challenge in League One as well.For more updates, subscribe to the BBC Sport newsletter for the latest news, features, and videos delivered straight to your inbox.

text: Sharks have patrolled the oceans for at least 400 million years and evolved into a huge range of remarkable species. Deep sea lantern sharks that shine in the dark, wobbegong sharks with their distinctive shaggy beards, and the majestic whale sharks, the ocean's largest fish, all capture the imagination. Yet, for many, the word shark conjures a single image: attacks. Despite the fear, the likelihood of encountering a shark, let alone being attacked, is remarkably low for beachgoers, divers, and surfers. In fact, lightning strikes, bee stings, and car accidents pose far greater risks. Ironically, humans kill millions more sharks than the reverse.A recent report by the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) reveals that a quarter of all shark species, along with their relatives, the rays, face the threat of extinction, primarily due to overfishing. The largest species are at the greatest risk. In Western Australia, a controversial shark cull was initiated following a series of attacks, sparking debate and protests.In response, scientists are exploring alternative methods to address shark attacks. At the forefront is Professor Shaun Collin from the University of Western Australia (UWA), leading a team of neurobiologists aiming to understand sharks' perspectives. We're trying to tread this very fine line of protecting both humans and sharks at the same time, Prof Collin explained on the BBC World Service programme Discovery. By examining shark brains and senses, the team is crafting non-lethal repellents to deter sharks from attacking humans.Among these innovations is a shark-proof wetsuit, designed to mimic the appearance of poisonous black and white banded sea snakes, which sharks tend to avoid. This concept, originally proposed by marine biologist Walter Starck, is being refined with insights into shark vision by the UWA team. Nathan Hart, an assistant professor at UWA, noted that sharks have poorer eyesight compared to humans. We've made sure that the size of the bands can be detected by a shark from a certain distance, he explained.The wetsuit's effectiveness is currently being tested by wrapping the fabric around a barrel filled with dead fish and observing sharks' reactions in the wild. Early results have been promising. Based on what we know about the sensory systems of sharks, they should reduce your risk to some extent, Nathan said. However, like a car seatbelt, it doesn't eliminate risk entirely but reduces it significantly.Another strategy involves designating shark-free zones for swimmers. We can try and define areas on the beaches where people are confident they can go and swim, Dr. Hart suggested. Bubble curtains, created by laying perforated hosepipes on the seabed and pumping air through them, could deter sharks from entering popular beaches. Sharks perceive these bubbles through sight, sound, and their lateral line, a sensory system for detecting vibrations and low-frequency sounds.Initial tests indicate that tiger sharks can eventually learn to cross bubble barriers, illustrating their capacity for learning. This concept was pioneered by Eugenie Clark, the Shark Lady, who in the 1950s demonstrated that sharks could learn and remember tasks. She once even transported a trained baby nurse shark as a gift for Japan's Crown Prince, with the shark occupying an extra airline seat.Recently, I experienced firsthand the ability of sharks to learn not to attack humans. Diving off Fiji, I encountered bull sharks, notorious for aggression, yet trained by Beqa Adventure Divers to approach divers calmly for food. They know us very well, Fijian divemaster Papa assured me. Observing these sharks up close, my initial apprehension vanished, replaced by awe at their grace and calm demeanor.These Fijian efforts not only challenge the perception of sharks as relentless killers but also highlight the economic value of live sharks over dead ones, especially given the pressures from the Asian demand for shark fin soup. Meanwhile, in Western Australia, the shark cull continues amid protests, driven by an unusual spike in attacks, with seven fatalities in three years compared to 20 in the previous century.The government's response involves setting baited hooks offshore, targeting great white, tiger, and bull sharks over 3m in length, which are then shot and discarded. Rodney Fox, a shark attack survivor turned advocate, criticizes this approach as unscientific and irrational. We just have to learn how to live with the sharks and not just kill them from fear, he stated.Despite opposition from over 100 scientists who have appealed to Premier Colin Barnett to reconsider the cull, citing its environmental impact and the low probability of targeting the responsible sharks, the government remains steadfast. The West Australian government is absolutely confident that the policy in place is the right policy and we intend to continue it, Barnett declared.

text: Poland's Prime Minister Beata Szydlo has vowed to press on with judicial reforms, saying the government would not yield to pressure from the street and from abroad.
