The European Commission had warned of potential sanctions if these changes proceeded, and European Council President Donald Tusk, a former Polish prime minister, cautioned against a black scenario that could marginalize Poland in Europe.Prime Minister Beata Szydlo, in a televised address, maintained that the ruling Law and Justice (PiS) party would persist with its judicial reforms. We all want to live in a fair Poland, which is why court reform is necessary, she declared. The president's veto has delayed this work. We cannot succumb to pressure from the streets or abroad. We have a stable majority and will not yield. We will implement our plan.President Duda, on national television, expressed his belief that the law would not enhance justice, stating, These laws must be amended. He vetoed two of the proposed laws but approved a third, granting the justice minister the authority to appoint heads of Poland's lower courts. This move surprised many, given Duda's previous affiliation with the right-wing ruling party advocating for the legislation.The PiS government dismissed claims that the reforms were authoritarian and expressed disappointment at Duda's veto. The president had already sought compromise the previous week, discussing the reforms with Zofia Romaszewska, a former dissident during Poland's communist era and now one of his advisers. Romaszewska, who was imprisoned during the martial law period of the early 1980s, advised against giving the attorney-general excessive control over the Supreme Court.Opposition MPs credited protesters with influencing the president's decision. A more plausible scenario involves redrafting the two vetoed bills in the coming weeks and seeking presidential approval. Meanwhile, the protest movement, celebrating its achievements, is urging Duda to veto the third reform as well.The outcome largely hinges on Jaroslaw Kaczynski, the PiS co-founder and perceived power behind the government.

text: Returning to Cold Feet after more than a decade since it was last seen on TV felt like putting on an old jumper, Fay Ripley has said. The actress expressed her excitement about stepping back into the shoes of Jenny, likening it to bumping into an old friend. Co-star John Thomson felt the timing was perfect for a revival, noting a great need for nostalgia in today's world. This autumn, viewers can look forward to eight new episodes of the comedy-drama, which originally concluded in 2003 after five successful series.The original series captivated over 10 million viewers in its final episode, which poignantly featured the funeral of central character Rachel, portrayed by Helen Baxendale. The upcoming series will explore the lives of friends Jenny and Pete, Karen and David, and widower Adam, as they navigate middle age and parenting teenagers.Ripley initially thought returning to her character might be challenging, but she quickly found herself back in the groove, saying, Within a minute, it was the same. It was like stepping back in time. We've got a shorthand when we work together, all of us, which is incredibly handy. She humorously added that this familiarity meant they could skip the formalities on set, quipping, You can just go in and say, 'I've got a banging headache, my menopause is giving me gip.'Thomson remarked that the timing couldn't be better for reviving something as uplifting as Cold Feet. He stated, The world isn't in a great place at the moment, and there's a great need for nostalgia, to look back at the days when things seemed okay.Hermione Norris shared that it was comforting to reunite the old characters but admitted she was initially hesitant about reprising her role as Karen. It's that thing in life - you think 'Don't go back, just move forward,' she explained. It was so of its time and it was so loved, I thought maybe it should be left as I didn't want to do anything that would have undone that. However, she was convinced by the show's creator, Mike Bullen, that this was not a remake but a chance to revisit these characters in this chapter of their life. She revealed that Karen uses Tinder in the new series, highlighting the evolution of technology and dating.Norris chose not to re-watch any old episodes before filming, noting, It was amazing how much I'd forgotten - I couldn't remember how many children David and I had. She also expressed missing Baxendale, saying, I missed Helen hugely - because Rachel was Karen's best friend. I really felt her absence. It's like it would be in real life if you've lost a really good friend.Ripley joked that there would be no shower moment for Rachel, referencing the infamous Dallas scene where Bobby Ewing's death was explained away as a dream. She added that Baxendale was happy with the show continuing without her, saying, She's cool with it.Norris also expressed her enjoyment of working with peers, stating, I really appreciate being with my own generation. As an actor, and as Karen. I find as a woman, I love being older. The weight of experience - you just don't have that as a 30-year-old.Robert Bathurst, who returns as David, attributed his decision to the quality of the script, saying, It's all very much down to the script. I wouldn't have done it for the sake of it. He believes the show's charm lies in its focus on ordinariness, adding, It's about people and how they rub along together. Bathurst hopes the new series will stand alone and draw in a new generation of fans.Joining the cast is BBC Radio 1 presenter Cel Spellman, who plays Adam and Rachel's teenage son Matthew, last seen as a baby. Spellman admitted feeling daunting joining the beloved show and binge-watched the box set to prepare. I started to realise why the show was so successful, he said, adding that his mother was a huge fan eager for storyline details.However, fans like Mrs. Spellman will have to wait to discover what's in store, as the show's creators are keen to avoid spoilers before the series airs. text: An electrical fire in a tunnel under a pavement in central London is still burning as firefighters have reported difficulty tackling the blaze. The London Fire Brigade (LFB) announced that firefighters would be engaged in efforts most of the night on Thursday as they continued to tackle a persistent fire that had been burning for over 24 hours. The fire, which was confined to a tunnel, prompted the evacuation of approximately 5,000 people from Holborn on Wednesday after smoke was seen billowing from an inspection cover. The incident has impacted more than 100 businesses in the area.Although the cordon around Kingsway has been reduced, the road remains closed, according to LFB. Assistant Commissioner Dany Cotton described the situation as a technically difficult and unusual incident to tackle as it is underground. She emphasized the hazards associated with fighting fires in tunnels and the precautions necessary to prevent a gas explosion. Firefighters have, however, been applying water through access points throughout the night, to control the spread of the fire, Cotton stated, urging the public to avoid the area if possible.A contingent of 35 firefighters and six fire engines are currently at the scene on Kingsway. Local road closures persist, and the cause of the blaze remains unknown, though it is suspected to have originated among underground cables.Speaking to BBC London 94.9, Met Police Inspector Neil Johnson remarked, I imagine this road will be closed a long time after this is finished because of damage the heat does to the road. It will have to remain closed until a structural engineer examines it properly and either he or she says what work has to be done and that work is completed - this is not an overnight job.Witnesses on Wednesday described the situation in Holborn as chaotic, with many struggling to breathe. UK Power Networks reported that around 1,000 customers were still affected by power cuts, although power had been restored to about 2,000. The company hopes to restore electricity to all affected customers by the end of Thursday. Matt Rudling from UK Power Networks apologized, stating, The gas is still burning under there and until we can gain access to that particular area we won't understand what's caused it and what we can do. He mentioned that emergency generators were being deployed to supply power and that engineers were attempting to connect damaged cables to those unaffected.The fire forced several West End theatres to cancel Wednesday evening performances, including shows like Beautiful - The Carole King Musical, Charlie And The Chocolate Factory, Disney's The Lion King, Gypsy, Mamma Mia!, The Play That Goes Wrong, and The Woman In Black. Matinee performances at the Novello and Aldwych theatres on Thursday were also called off.Councillor Richard Beddoe of Westminster City Council expressed relief that there were no serious casualties but criticized the impact on major businesses in the West End due to inadequate infrastructure, demanding action.The National Grid is collaborating with emergency services to isolate the gas supply. In a statement, the company explained that the fire affected one of its pipes, and due to the fire's location and proximity to other utilities, the operation is challenging. We cannot just turn a valve and switch off the gas because of safety reasons and [the] impact on the gas network, the statement read.Transport for London confirmed that Holborn station remains open, but nine bus services—1, 59, 68, 91, 168, 171, 188, 243, and 521—are being diverted. For the latest travel updates, follow @BBCTravelAlert on Twitter and visit the BBC London Travel website.

text: US illustrator Norman Bridwell, creator of the Clifford the Big Red Dog books, has died at the age of 86 following a fall at his home in Massachusetts. The beloved character of Clifford, the big red dog, first bounded onto the scene in 1963, capturing hearts in over 40 stories and selling an astounding 120 million copies globally. Clifford's iconic image has also graced various merchandise and even made appearances in notable US landmarks, including the White House. Norman Bridwell, Clifford's creator, had completed two additional books slated for release next year. Dick Robinson, president of Scholastic, the author's long-time publisher, expressed his sorrow, saying, We are deeply saddened by the loss of our loyal and talented friend whose drawings and stories have inspired all of us and generations of children and their parents.Norma, Bridwell's wife of 56 years, remarked, A lot of people were Clifford fans and that makes them Norman fans too. She had named the character Clifford after her imaginary childhood friend. Over the years, Clifford starred in numerous tales, such as Clifford Goes To Hollywood and Clifford and The Grouchy Neighbours, becoming a staple of bedtime stories for children across the US and beyond. The lovable dog often found himself in trouble but would redeem himself through daring rescues or good deeds.Norma Bridwell noted similarities between her husband and his creation, saying, He's never been able to recognize that. Clifford tries to do the right thing, Norman tries to do the right thing, and he makes a mess of it. But he's the most lovable grown-up man. He's just a nice guy.Before Clifford brought him fame, Bridwell worked as a commercial artist in the 1950s. He faced numerous rejections in his attempts to break into children's publishing until a New York book editor suggested he craft a story around an illustration he had submitted of a child with her oversized dog. Despite further rejections, Scholastic recognized the potential of his creation, leading to enduring success for both Bridwell and the company.Reflecting on his early success, Bridwell once told his wife, Now don't count on there being any more. This one is just a fluke. I don't know if there will ever be another one. In later years, Clifford was animated in a television cartoon series in the US, and a feature film, Clifford's Big Red Movie, was released in 2004.Bridwell leaves behind his wife, a son, and three grandchildren. His family announced that a small private funeral service is planned, along with a more public celebration of his life and work.

text: Residents of a mid Wales village have voted on proposals to install a new train station in the area. The Welsh Government has tasked the Carno Station Action Group and the local community council with gathering residents' opinions on two potential sites for a new station. One proposed location is the original Carno station, which was closed in 1963 due to the Beeching cuts that affected Britain's railways. This historic site later became part of the Laura Ashley complex in Carno. The village, situated on the Cambrian line between Aberystwyth and Shrewsbury, has seen a campaign for the station's reopening since 2002.In 2011, Mid Wales Transportation, collaborating with the Welsh Government, conducted an appraisal that highlighted a compelling case for investing in the station's future. Should the plans proceed, the site could transform into a tourist information center and a museum dedicated to Laura Ashley.Jeremy Barnes, chairman of the Action Group, announced that the week-long consultation concluded on March 22. The findings will be reviewed before submission to the Welsh Government. He noted, We've discussed with the Welsh government the potential for the new station to include a tourist information center, a cafe, an office for the community council's clerk, and a small Laura Ashley museum if the current site is selected.Barnes emphasized the benefits, stating, Carno is a growing village with around 750 residents. This development will create jobs and provide affordable travel options for work beyond the village. He added, It is located on Wales' longest railway stretch without an intermediate stop, spanning 22 miles between Caersws and Machynlleth. There is a strong feeling that the railway line's potential is being squandered as trains pass through without stopping.This consultation follows a meeting last October between the action group and Transport Minister Edwina Hart. Fashion designer Laura Ashley had deep ties to Carno for nearly 25 years before her passing in 1985. Carno served as the original Welsh base for the Laura Ashley company when she and her husband, Bernard, relocated from Kent in 1961. She is laid to rest in the village churchyard. The former headquarters of Laura Ashley in Carno, where many of her designs were produced, closed its doors in 2004.

text: A US Senate report has condemned the CIA's use of enhanced interrogation on al-Qaeda suspects after the 9/11 attacks. A newly released 480-page summary sheds light on the harsh treatment faced by key figures within a notorious organization. Recently, details about the interrogations of three prominent individuals have been unveiled. Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, Abu Zubaydah, and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, all captured following the 9/11 attacks, are currently detained at Guantanamo Bay.Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, once labeled by US intelligence as one of history's most infamous terrorists, has admitted to orchestrating the 9/11 attacks. He also claims to have personally executed US journalist Daniel Pearl. Born in Kuwait to Pakistani parents, Mohammed pursued higher education in the United States before joining the fight against the Soviets in Afghanistan, where he is believed to have first encountered Osama Bin Laden. His involvement in numerous plots, including a 1995 plan to bomb US airlines over the Pacific, is well-documented. After his 2003 capture in Pakistan, Mohammed was transferred to detention centers, reportedly in Europe, where he endured waterboarding at least 183 times. A CIA officer described the method as a series of near drownings, though the Senate report indicates some information he provided was fabricated. Efforts to try him in a New York court were thwarted by significant opposition, and he remains at Guantanamo Bay.Abu Zubaydah, thought to have been al-Qaeda's chief recruiter in the 1990s, later emerged as a vital organizer connecting Osama Bin Laden with other al-Qaeda cells. Although not directly linked to the 9/11 attacks, Zubaydah is believed to have managed several Afghan training camps used by the attackers. Born in Saudi Arabia, he adopted over 30 aliases and became known for his ability to disguise himself. Captured in Pakistan in 2002 and taken to a detention camp reportedly in Thailand, US intelligence at the time accused him of planning a terror attack in Israel. He endured enhanced interrogation techniques for prolonged periods, including more than 80 instances of waterboarding. One report describes him as being left completely unresponsive with bubbles rising through his open full mouth. The Senate report reveals Zubaydah spent 266 hours in a confined space scarcely larger than a coffin and 29 hours in an even smaller box measuring 21 inches wide and 2.5 feet deep and tall. It was found that US Justice Department lawyers relied on inaccurate CIA information to justify harsh treatment. Zubaydah is currently held at Guantanamo Bay.Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri gained notoriety as the alleged mastermind behind the attack on the USS Cole, a US destroyer targeted by suicide bombers in Aden, Yemen. US intelligence identified the Saudi-born Islamist as the leader of al-Qaeda's Gulf operations. Beyond the USS Cole attack, which resulted in the deaths of 17 sailors, he was suspected of plotting against Western targets in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the Straits of Gibraltar, Morocco, and Qatar. Allegedly, he fought with the Taliban in Afghanistan and participated in earlier Chechen and Tajik insurgencies. Arrested in Dubai in 2002, al-Nashiri was detained in various secret CIA facilities worldwide, including in Poland and Thailand, where he faced waterboarding and mock executions. He was transferred to Guantanamo Bay in 2006, where he remains incarcerated.

text: Scotland prop Alasdair Dickinson is braced for a bruising encounter with the Japan pack on Saturday. An Edinburgh veteran has downplayed the impression that last year's 45-10 victory at the World Cup was as easy as the scoreline suggests. We know they are coming after revenge from the World Cup, so it will be a tough one, he stated. Their front five are all big, strong men, and for us, it is another battle we have to win.The Scots are set to begin a two-Test tour in Toyota City, facing hosts ranked just one spot below them at 10th in the world rankings. Reflecting on September's triumph at Kingsholm, the Scots managed to score five second-half tries against a weary opponent, who had previously shocked South Africa in their opening game. They had been outstanding against South Africa and were backing up that performance four days later, recalled 32-year-old Dickinson. I found it very hard, especially up front. They are very strong men, well-drilled, and enjoy their scrummaging. I expect it to be equally hard at the weekend.He emphasized the need for a strong start, a lesson learned from their previous encounter. We need to start well, which we did not do particularly well in that game. We need to tidy up a few of our fundamentals and need to come out of the box firing. Japan takes their chances. They are very skillful players, and we have seen what happens when they capitalize on errors with a lot of broken field play. Minimize errors and start better.Historically, Scotland has never lost to Japan, who will be missing their World Cup captain Michael Leitch and key goal kicker Ayumu Goromaru. Despite perceptions of Japan's scrum as a weak point, Dickinson cautions that Scotland must remain vigilant. All the games I have watched Japan play over many years, their set piece has been excellent, he commented. We saw in the World Cup the tight areas were a huge challenge for us. Japan will have progressed, as have we - it is an area they are targeting.He further noted, The Japanese scrum is probably the lowest in the world. It is probably how they are built, big men who can get really low, and we have to manage the combat. They are a tough scrummaging team who will be coming for us. It will be a good challenge.

text: France rounded off their Euro 2016 preparations with a classy and comprehensive victory over Scotland. In a commanding display, Didier Deschamps' team showcased why they are considered pre-tournament favorites. Olivier Giroud silenced his critics by netting the first two goals, while his Arsenal teammate Laurent Koscielny added a third with a header before halftime. Although the second half saw a flurry of substitutions that disrupted the rhythm, Scotland managed to escape with some dignity intact.While this match didn't definitively answer questions about France's potential, the hosts of the tournament certainly demonstrated their quality. Their midfield, featuring the formidable trio of N'Golo Kante, Paul Pogba, and Blaise Matuidi, was a powerhouse of strength and athleticism. Despite facing boos and criticism from French fans and media ahead of the Euros, Giroud's clever back-heel and quick reflexes on a close-range rebound earned him a standing ovation from the crowd in Metz.Deschamps also gave playing time to Kingsley Coman, Dimitri Payet, Antoine Griezmann, and Anthony Martial as he assessed his options ahead of Friday's match against Romania in Paris. Although concerns linger about the strength of France's defense, Scotland posed no real challenge in that regard.Gordon Strachan lamented his team's inability to pass and control the ball following a 1-0 loss to Italy, and this game offered little improvement. Though they had more possession than against the Italians, the Scots rarely used it effectively and failed to register a shot on target once again. Goalkeeper David Marshall, as he had done six days earlier, minimized the damage with a series of impressive saves, solidifying his position for the World Cup qualifiers starting in September.A glimmer of hope for the Scottish side came from young Swansea full-back Stephen Kingsley, who delivered an assured performance in the second half. Rangers winger Barrie McKay also made his senior international debut off the bench. Pogba dominated the game, coming close to adding a fourth goal twice, first hitting the post with a powerful free-kick, then curling another shot onto the roof of the net.The match concluded with France triumphing 3-0 over Scotland. In the second half, Antoine Griezmann's header from the center of the box went too high, assisted by Bacary Sagna's cross. A corner was conceded by Ikechi Anya, and Moussa Sissoko replaced N'Golo Kanté for France. Steven Naismith's right-footed shot from outside the box for Scotland was narrowly high, assisted by Barrie McKay.Fouls and substitutions punctuated the game, with Lucas Digne replacing Patrice Evra for France and Barrie McKay coming on for James McArthur for Scotland. Yohan Cabaye's shot from the center of the box was too high, assisted by Pogba. Pogba's free-kick from outside the box also went just over the bar. Griezmann won a free kick in the attacking half, after being fouled by Charlie Mulgrew, while Stephen Kingsley earned a free kick in the defensive half for Scotland.Hugo Lloris secured a free kick in the defensive half for France after a foul by Steven Naismith. A corner for Scotland was conceded by Patrice Evra. Yohan Cabaye's shot from outside the box was saved by the Scottish goalkeeper, assisted by Anthony Martial. Pogba won another free kick in the defensive half following a foul by McArthur.Further substitutions saw Yohan Cabaye replace Blaise Matuidi for France, while Stephen Kingsley swapped in for Robert Snodgrass for Scotland. Anthony Martial's shot from the center of the box missed to the left, assisted by Matuidi. Adil Rami's left-footed attempt was saved in the top left corner. Pogba's powerful free-kick struck the left post. André-Pierre Gignac replaced Giroud for France, and Matuidi won a free kick in the attacking half after McArthur's foul.Corners for France were conceded by David Marshall and McArthur, while Pogba's shot from outside the box was blocked, assisted by Matuidi. Steven Naismith replaced Steven Fletcher for Scotland, and Griezmann's left-footed shot from outside the box was blocked, assisted by Pogba. Olivier Giroud committed a foul, giving McArthur a free kick on the right wing. Steven Fletcher's header from the center of the box missed to the right, assisted by Anya's cross. Rami's header from the center of the box also missed to the right, assisted by Griezmann following a corner.

text: The body set up to probe deaths during the Troubles in Northern Ireland investigated cases where the state was involved with less rigour than others, a police watchdog has found. The HM Inspectorate of Constabulary has criticized the Historical Enquiries Team (HET) for basing its policies on a misrepresentation of the law, leading to inconsistent approaches and significant shortcomings. Established in 2005, the HET was tasked with re-examining 3,260 murder cases from the Troubles. However, the report highlighted that the HET's handling of state-involved cases was inconsistent with the European Convention on Human Rights.Stephen Otter, Her Majesty's Inspector of Constabulary, expressed concerns about the legality of the HET's actions. We believe it was acting unlawfully regarding state cases because it treated them differently in policy and practice, he stated. This differential treatment rendered state cases less effective, failing the crucial test of Article 2 compliance. The HMIC warned that such practices could erode the trust of the victims' families in the HET’s impartiality and effectiveness.The review was commissioned by Northern Ireland's Chief Constable Matt Baggott, following a request from the policing board and criticism from a University of Ulster report by Dr. Patricia Lundy. Lundy's report accused the HET of giving preferential treatment to former soldiers and inadequately investigating military-related deaths, claims the HET had previously rejected.Dr. Lundy, responding to the HMIC report, declared the HET irretrievable and criticized its lack of oversight and complaints procedures. It seemed to me a bit of a law unto itself, she remarked. Otter acknowledged that Lundy's findings, initially dismissed in 2009, deserved an apology from the Chief Constable on behalf of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI). For four years, these findings were ignored, which is hard to believe, he added.Chief Constable Baggott announced that all military cases investigated by the HET would be re-examined, admitting that HET put in place a policy that was wrong. He assured that the differential approach to military cases had ended and committed to implementing the HMIC's recommendations fully. The HET is currently reviewing over 150 killings by soldiers between 1970 and September 1973.The HMIC's inspection assessed whether the HET's review of military cases adhered to current policing standards. The analysis covered 31 cases previously reviewed by the HET, revealing a policy-driven disparity in how military cases were treated. The report pointed out a lack of explicit systems, inconsistent working practices across teams, no defined complaints process, and the absence of an independent review until now.The report also criticized the HET for not consistently verifying claims of interviewee unfitness due to illness in state involvement cases, which led to a less rigorous review of military cases. Notably, since 2010, none of the 39 cases referred back to the PSNI involved state actors. It's striking that not one state involvement case relating to the British Army has been referred for further investigation or prosecution, the report noted.Otter expressed concern that these inconsistencies might undermine the HET's ability to assess whether force used in state-involved killings during the Troubles was justified. This could hinder the identification and prosecution of those responsible. He emphasized the need for fundamental improvements to ensure the HET meets Article 2 requirements and maintains public confidence, especially among the victims' families.Operating in an extraordinarily complex social and political context, Otter stressed the importance of the HET maintaining high standards of effectiveness and impartiality. The HMIC interviewed over 180 individuals from various organizations, including HET members, criminal justice agencies, and non-governmental bodies, as well as families of 13 victims in Belfast and Londonderry.Despite calls for the HET to be independent from the PSNI, there remains a strong desire for its continuation, provided operational improvements are made. As a special investigative unit linked to the PSNI, the HET is responsible for re-examining the deaths of thousands in Northern Ireland between 1968 and 1998, maintaining direct accountability to Northern Ireland's Chief Constable.

text: Progressive music, the oft-maligned genre that had its heyday in the 1970s, is to be endorsed by the Official Charts Company (OCC). Next week marks a significant moment in music history with the unveiling of the first-ever monthly Official Progressive Albums Chart Top 30. While legendary prog bands like Pink Floyd will feature, the number one spot is claimed by the 21st-century rock sensation Tame Impala. We felt it was an oversight not to have done this a long time ago, commented Martin Talbot, head of the Official Charts Company. Progressive music is as vibrant as ever, more a mindset than a mere genre.This chart debut aligns with the annual Progressive Music Awards, set to take place at Shakespeare's Globe Theatre in London on Thursday night. The event will honor Genesis founding member Tony Banks with the 2015 Prog God Award. Rick Wakeman, who earned this title in 2012, expressed to the BBC that a dedicated chart for progressive music was long overdue. It's only 45 years too late, but better late than never, remarked the former Yes keyboardist. Prog rock is thriving... the musicianship among young bands today surpasses that of the 1970s.The upcoming issue of Prog Magazine will showcase the first official progressive album chart, with Tame Impala's Currents leading, followed by Muse's Drones.Rick Wakeman praised the diversity of prog rock, stating, It shows that wonderful wide spectrum that prog rock has got. It's no longer something to be sneered at. With so many bands drawing from it, it's widely accepted as a genuine contributor to the modern music scene.Emerging from the psychedelic sounds of the 1960s, prog rock was initially linked to bands like Pink Floyd, Rush, Genesis, Yes, and King Crimson. It saw a resurgence in the 1980s with acts like Marillion, while contemporary bands such as Muse, The Mars Volta, and Porcupine Tree continue to carry the torch.Jerry Ewing, editor of Prog Magazine, noted, Prog artists have always pushed the boundaries of musical convention, becoming some of the best-selling and most influential artists of all time. Prog didn't stop in the 1970s; many people are into prog artists without realizing it. Modern icons like Muse, Radiohead, Mogwai, and Tame Impala are challenging themselves and inspiring new generations. The Official Progressive Albums Chart will acknowledge this.The last chart introduced by the Official Chart Company was the vinyl chart in spring 2015. The new progressive chart joins other genres like dance, urban, jazz, blues, and country. The monthly Top 30 will rank the best-selling titles based on physical and digital sales, alongside audio streaming data.There are artists who embrace the term 'progressive,' while others shy away from it due to its past stigma, explained Martin Talbot. The punk wars aimed to eliminate prog music, but it was prog and disco that ultimately triumphed—perhaps even more than punk.To celebrate the chart's launch, the Official Charts Company has compiled a list of the top-selling prog artists of the 21st century, highlighting their most successful albums. The list is provided below.Official Progressive Artist Chart of the 21st Century - Top 10 © Official Charts Company 2015

text: Kenyan officials say the country is closing its borders to travellers from Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone in response to the deadly Ebola outbreak. Kenya's Health Secretary has confirmed that both Kenyans and medical personnel arriving from certain states will still be permitted entry. Meanwhile, Kenyan Airways has announced its decision to halt flights to Liberia and Sierra Leone, effective Wednesday, in response to a travel ban. The World Health Organization (WHO) has identified Kenya as being at high risk for Ebola due to its status as a major transport hub.The Ebola epidemic, which originated in Guinea in February, has since extended its reach to Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Nigeria. As of Friday, the death toll climbed to 1,145, following the report of 76 new fatalities within the two days leading up to August 13. The total number of cases has reached 2,127.Kenya's health ministry previously reported that four suspected Ebola cases in the country tested negative. These cases involved a Liberian national, two Nigerians who had recently traveled to Kenya, and a Zimbabwean.Following advice from the Kenyan government, Kenyan Airways decided to cancel flights to the capitals of Liberia and Sierra Leone. Passengers affected by the suspension will receive full refunds. Notably, flights to Nigeria remain unaffected by this decision.Kenyan Health Minister James Macharia announced the government's move, emphasizing it was made in the interest of public health. He cautioned that strict checks would be implemented for Kenyans and health workers returning from the three West African nations, with quarantine measures enforced if deemed necessary.On Friday, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) stated that controlling the outbreak would take at least six months. MSF President Joanne Liu remarked that the situation is deteriorating faster, and moving faster, than we can respond to. The WHO also acknowledged that the outbreak's scale seems vastly underestimated, calling for extraordinary measures to contain it.Ebola is spread through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected individual. Initial symptoms resemble the flu but can escalate to external bleeding from the eyes and gums, and internal hemorrhaging, potentially leading to organ failure. Despite these risks, the WHO maintains that the likelihood of Ebola transmission during air travel remains low.

text: Leaving the EU without a trade deal would be irresponsible, the president of the CBI business group will warn. Paul Drechsler is set to express his agreement with the Prime Minister that a deal with the EU is achievable, but he criticizes those suggesting that the only option is to leave without one as wrong. He will highlight that both UK and European businesses dread this worst-case scenario.The pro-Brexit group Change Britain has accused the CBI of repeatedly being proven wrong on Europe and urged it to adopt a more optimistic outlook regarding the UK’s future. Drechsler's upcoming speech in London echoes recent warnings from the British Chambers of Commerce and former Chancellor George Osborne.Drechsler will affirm that the business community backs the government's pursuit of an ambitious trade agreement and that the CBI is collaborating with business groups across the EU to secure a mutually beneficial deal. To those who advocate for Britain to walk away without a deal, I say you're not only wrong but irresponsible, he plans to assert.He warns that if the UK defaults to World Trade Organisation trading rules due to a lack of an EU deal, British companies could face tariffs on 90% of their exports to the EU, along with additional regulatory hurdles impacting firms across Europe. He acknowledges that while some businesses are bracing for this worst-case scenario, others find the preparation costs prohibitive.Theresa May has committed to triggering Article 50 by the end of the month. Although she is determined to secure a favorable agreement, she has also stated, no deal is better than a bad deal. Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson has expressed confidence that the UK can be ever-more European and ever-more internationalist simultaneously, suggesting that a win-win EU deal is feasible within the two-year Brexit negotiation window.Drechsler emphasizes that achieving a smooth Brexit is in everyone's interest. However, Change Britain's spokesperson, Chloe Westley, criticizes the CBI, recalling its past support for joining the euro and its warnings of economic disaster if the UK left the EU. She insists, It has been proven wrong time and again on Europe, and there is no reason to suggest this has changed. Westley argues that it is in the EU's best interest to establish a free trade agreement with the UK and urges the CBI to support the government in securing the best deal for Britain.Patrick Minford, chairman of Economists for Brexit, challenges the assumption that Brexit without an EU trade deal would harm the UK. Our research shows that if the UK removes all import tariffs, even without EU reciprocation, we could add 4% to GDP and 7.3% to UK treasury receipts compared to the status quo, he claims. Our economy can and will thrive outside the single market, and a trade deal with the EU is not necessary to achieve that.

text: A man soldiered on after a serious and brutal hammer attack by a friend before dying five days later, a court was told. Cambridge Crown Court was the setting for a harrowing case where Mitchell Bird was accused of assaulting Bradley Carter at a Wisbech flat on February 14. During the proceedings, the jury learned that Carter, aged 35, experienced pain following the incident and was taken to the hospital by his mother on February 19. Tragically, he collapsed and died shortly thereafter.Mitchell Bird, 29, residing at Cox Close, Wisbech, has pleaded not guilty to murder. Prosecutor Richard Christie QC revealed that Carter had sought refuge at Bird's flat after being expelled from his mother's home due to his drug use. Both men were known to be regular drug users, the court heard.On the night of the assault, neighbors reported a disturbance, and Bird allegedly accused Carter of attempted theft. The prosecution presented evidence that Carter had claimed Bird beat him repeatedly with a hammer, leading to holes in his legs. Photographs of Carter's injuries, taken by him and his mother in the days following the attack, were shown to the jury.Christie further explained that Carter had an enlarged spleen protruding beyond his ribcage, which was damaged during this attack from kicks to his body. This damage resulted in internal bleeding and a ruptured spleen, ultimately leading to his death.Carter had voiced his suffering from the attack to friends, family, a probation officer, and a housing officer. On February 19, his mother, Helen Barnes, took him to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn due to his worsening condition and significant back pain. However, when she returned from paying the parking meter, she found that her son had collapsed and died.Despite the time lapse between the attack and Carter's death, Christie asserted, Although there was a delay in Bradley Carter dying, this defendant murdered him. He emphasized, We have clear evidence in this case that points to Mitchell Bird having perpetrated that assault.Bird faces charges of murder and grievous bodily harm with intent, both of which he denies. The trial is ongoing and is expected to continue for two weeks.

text: On Friday 11 May 2012, Derby woke up to the news there had been a fire at a house in the Allenton area. What transformed them in the eyes of the police from grieving parents to suspects capable of such a heinous act?During their trial at Nottingham Crown Court, tapes revealed a chaotic scene on Victory Road the night of the fire. Mick Philpott was heard frantically pleading with emergency services: Help me! My babies are trapped inside! The couple insisted they had been asleep in the downstairs conservatory when the fire erupted. Meanwhile, their six children, Duwayne, 13, Jade, 10, John, nine, Jack, eight, Jesse, six, and Jayden, five, were upstairs.Philpott claimed he attempted a rescue using a ladder, in what Derbyshire Police described as apparent valiant attempts. However, Det Supt Kate Meynell began hearing a different narrative from neighbors who also tried to save the children. Within a few days, they commented on how they felt they were making more effort to rescue the children and that Michael Philpott was not as instrumental as he should have been, she noted.The fire, determined to be arson, started in the hallway beneath the letterbox, where petrol had been poured. A petrol can and a glove found near Victory Road were collected as evidence. The investigation initially focused on those close to the family, ruling out a man Philpott had previously assaulted. Assistant Chief Constable Steve Cotterill remarked on Mick Philpott's demeanor, describing it as the most astonishing behavior he had seen in 30 years of policing. I would have expected him to be completely and utterly destroyed, he said, noting it appeared as though Philpott was acting. Covert recordings in the couple's hotel room provided crucial evidence. When I first expressed my desire to attend university, a teacher suggested I lower my ambitions and consider hairdressing.When Judge Dhir was called to the bar in 1989, the legal profession was predominantly male, white, and filled with individuals from public schools with connections to the field. That's four differences before even starting, she noted. Moreover, most clients were reluctant to have a young Asian Scottish female advocate, complicating my efforts to establish a client base.Recalling an incident, she said she once had to show her wig and gown to gain entry into court. text: Doctors who carry out cosmetic procedures should give patients time to think before agreeing to go ahead, new guidance says. The General Medical Council (GMC) has introduced new guidelines aimed at enhancing the safety of both surgical and non-surgical cosmetic procedures, including facelifts, breast implants, dermal fillers, and Botox. This initiative will now move to a consultation phase involving both doctors and the public.Plastic surgeons have noted that they have already implemented a two-week cooling-off period for patients considering cosmetic surgery. This practice gained attention following a 2013 report by NHS England's medical director, which underscored the risks within the cosmetic sector. This report came in the wake of safety concerns affecting nearly 50,000 women in the UK who received PIP breast implants. These French implants, made with unauthorized silicone filler, had a rupture rate twice that of other implants.In January, the Royal College of Surgeons launched a consultation on proposals to elevate standards in cosmetic surgery. The GMC is responsible for setting the expectations for UK doctors performing cosmetic procedures and aims to help patients understand what they should expect from their healthcare providers.Key points in the new guidance emphasize that doctors should not rush patients into decisions they might regret. Prof Terence Stephenson, chairman of the GMC, stressed the importance of protecting vulnerable patients in this field. We are clear that doctors must not pressure patients to make rushed decisions they may end up regretting and they must give them enough information so they can make an informed choice, he stated.Rajiv Grover, a consultant plastic surgeon and former President of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (Baaps), expressed support for the GMC's guidelines. He pointed out that some patients are psychologically unsuitable for cosmetic surgery. Cosmetic surgery has for too long been seen as a commodity but unfortunately once an operation is done - it can't be taken back to the shop, Grover remarked. Baaps has long advocated for a two-week cooling-off period and recommends a second consultation with a surgeon before making a final decision. The association is also working on developing a screening tool to identify patients who should avoid surgery.The final version of the GMC's guidance is anticipated to be released in early 2016.

text: A teenager has been detained for a sex attack on a student who went on to publish an open letter about the ordeal. Last month, Oxford University student Ione Wells, aged 20, was assaulted while walking home near Camden. Her attacker, a 17-year-old whose identity remains undisclosed, received a two-year youth detention sentence at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court. Having confessed to the sexual assault in a previous hearing, he was informed that he would serve half of this sentence under supervision. Furthermore, he will be listed on the sex offenders register for five years.During the court proceedings, it was revealed that the teenager had approached Ms. Wells from behind, forcefully pushing her to the ground and causing her head to strike the pavement. He then assaulted her with such aggression that her bra was torn apart. In a poignant victim impact statement, Ms. Wells described the attack as the most traumatic event of her life, leaving her feeling tainted and violated. She also recounted experiencing flashbacks and the haunting sound of footsteps.In the defense's mitigation, the teenager's lawyer claimed that the young man deeply regrets his actions and is willing to prove that this incident will not be repeated. However, the judge emphasized the severity of the attack and its profound psychological impact on Ms. Wells, deeming a custodial sentence necessary.Ms. Wells, choosing to forgo her right to anonymity, shared her story publicly by publishing a powerful letter to her attacker in the student newspaper, Cherwell. She expressed that the overwhelming positive feedback she received had transformed what was an incredibly hurtful experience. In her letter, she declared: My community will not feel we are unsafe walking back home after dark. We will get on the last Tube home, and we will walk up our streets alone, because we will not ingrain or submit to the idea that we are putting ourselves in danger in doing so. Your community - even if you can't see it around you every day. It is there. It is everywhere.The aftermath of the attack and the publication of her letter inspired Ms. Wells to launch the #NotGuilty campaign, advocating that victims in sexual assault cases should never be held accountable for the crimes against them. The Crown Prosecution Service praised Ms. Wells for her bravery, stating that she had shown real courage throughout this case, this was a terrifying attack which no one should have to experience.

text: Careers services for young people in England need to be urgently improved, says a report from an advisory body set up by the government. The National Careers Council has issued a stark warning about the inadequacies in the current state of career guidance for young people, highlighting a troubling inconsistency and lack of availability across the UK. Deirdre Hughes, who chaired the council, emphasized the urgent need for a culture change in careers provision.The council's report reveals massive variations in career advice access, heavily dependent on geographic location. In one region, there are as many as 134 advisory services, while another has only a single service. This disparity leaves many young people without the guidance they need to make informed decisions about their futures.Concerns have also been raised about the National Careers Service, which is primarily structured to cater to adults, thereby neglecting the needs of school-age individuals. While the service conducts over a million face-to-face sessions for adults annually, young people are limited to phone advice lines and online resources, lacking personalized support.Expressing disappointment with the slow progress in enhancing careers services for the youth, the council advocates for the establishment of an employer-led advisory body to oversee the development of a more effective system. It also urges the government to ensure all schools have free or subsidized access to independent and impartial career development resources. Furthermore, the council recommends creating a fund to expand successful career advice models across various schools and regions.The quality of career provision has been under scrutiny, with multiple critical reports casting doubt on the decision to transfer advisory responsibilities to individual schools. Last year, Ofsted chief Sir Michael Wilshaw expressed concern over the failure of new arrangements to deliver adequate guidance, noting that many schools lacked the expertise to provide high-quality advice. The Education Select Committee echoed these sentiments, reporting a worrying deterioration in career services.Neil Carberry of the CBI criticized the shift of responsibility to schools as a failure, stressing that schools, government, and businesses must collaborate to address the issue, as schools cannot bear the burden alone. Brian Lightman, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, acknowledged the efforts of schools but noted that many are finding it extremely difficult to provide effective career guidance.The situation has created a stark postcode lottery, according to head teachers' leader, leaving young people at a disadvantage. Nick Chambers, director of the Education and Employers Taskforce charity, lamented that too many youths are forced to make critical life decisions without access to reliable information.Despite some progress over the past year, Hughes remarked that it has been far too slow, leaving the education and labor markets complex and confusing for young people, parents, and teachers, with significant costs attached. She called for immediate action across England to prevent further decline in youth career services.Labour's shadow education secretary, Tristram Hunt, criticized the government's handling of career services, stating, There is surely no other policy agenda where the government has so miserably failed our young people. He proposed reversing the decision to make work experience placements optional and advocated for each school to have a governor dedicated to fostering connections with local businesses to enhance career advice and work experience opportunities.

text: A botnet which experts believe sent out 18% of the world's spam email has been shut down, a security firm said. Grum's command servers, primarily located in Panama, Russia, and Ukraine, have been dismantled. This decisive action was the result of a concerted effort by security firm FireEye and spam-tracking service SpamHaus, who collaborated with local internet service providers (ISPs) to dismantle the illegal network. A botnet, such as Grum, is a network of computers commandeered by cybercriminals, typically through malicious software. Atif Mushtaq, a security researcher at FireEye, emphasized the collective effort involved in Grum's takedown, stating, Grum's takedown resulted from the efforts of many individuals. He added, This collaboration is sending a strong message to all the spammers: Stop sending us spam. We don't need your cheap Viagra or fake Rolex.Mushtaq recounted that on Monday, a Dutch server linked to Grum was shut down, which he noted at least made a dent in the botnet. By Tuesday, the command and control servers in Panama were also disabled. However, this victory was short-lived. This good news was soon followed by some bad news, Mushtaq explained. The bot herders, upon realizing the Panamanian server was offline, swiftly redirected the remaining command and control servers to new locations in Ukraine. At one point, I was thinking that all we needed was to take down one Russian server, but right in front of my eyes, the bot herders started pointing their botnet to new destinations, he said. Historically, Ukraine has been viewed as a safe haven for such activities, with Mushtaq acknowledging, Shutting down any servers there has never been easy.The dismantling of Grum is part of a broader initiative to neutralize botnets globally. In May, Russian national Georgiy Avanesov was sentenced to four years in prison for orchestrating the Bredolab botnet, which reportedly generated over £80,000 monthly. Meanwhile, Microsoft has been actively working to disrupt Zeus, another extensive network implicated in thefts amounting to millions of pounds.FireEye, alongside global security experts, pressured local ISPs to cease the illegal operations. Mushtaq reported that although more than 20,000 computers remain in the botnet, they will soon be ineffective without active command and control servers. He described Grum's closure as a positive step in the global fight against botnets. When the appropriate channels are used, even ISPs within Russia and Ukraine can be pressured to end their cooperation with bot herders, Mushtaq asserted. He added, There are no longer any safe havens. Most of the spam botnets that used to keep their CnCs in the USA and Europe have moved to countries like Panama, Russia, and Ukraine thinking that no one can touch them in these comfort zones. We have proven them wrong this time. Keep on dreaming of a junk-free inbox.

text: Former Arkansas Governor Mike Huckabee has launched a second attempt at getting the Republican nomination for the presidency. In his hometown of Hope, Arkansas, Mike Huckabee launched his presidential campaign with the slogan hope to higher ground. Known for his bass guitar skills and hawkish foreign policy stance, Huckabee has maintained a media presence since his unsuccessful 2008 nomination bid. He now enters a crowded Republican race featuring three senators, a businesswoman, and a neurosurgeon.Folks, it is a long way from a little brick rent house on Second Street in Hope, Arkansas, to the White House, Huckabee declared. Here in this small town called Hope, I was raised to believe that where a person started didn't mean that's where he had to stop. I always believed that a kid could go from Hope to higher ground. His announcement was met with enthusiastic chants of We want Mike! from the crowd.The former Southern Baptist minister, who received a BB gun at age five, reiterated his pro-gun stance. He also called for the abolition of the US Department of Education, aligning with conservatives critical of recent national education reforms. On immigration, Huckabee emphasized the need for secure borders but offered few specifics. He also reaffirmed his opposition to same-sex marriage.Mike Huckabee is making a comeback. Eight years ago, he staged a surprisingly strong presidential run, finishing second to Arizona Senator John McCain and winning the Iowa caucuses along with seven other states. In 2012, despite speculation and favorable polls, Huckabee, then a television and radio host, chose not to run, saying his heart says no.Now, however, Huckabee's heart has changed its tune. Abandoning his media roles, he joins the 2016 race, facing a more competitive field than he would have in 2012. This field includes candidates who will vie for the evangelical support that fueled his 2008 campaign. Huckabee brings to the table name recognition, a solid fundraising network, and prior campaign experience. Yet, with formidable Republican opponents who are equally engaging and well-funded, the question remains: will it be enough?Reflecting on his background, Huckabee noted he was the first male in his family to graduate high school. My dad wasn't an educated man, but he was a smart man. And he and my mother didn't have a whole lot, but they had honesty to the bone, he said.As his campaign unfolds, Huckabee may face criticism within his party. Many conservatives are displeased that taxes and spending increased during his tenure as Arkansas governor. In 2008, Huckabee secured eight primaries in socially conservative states, but this time he pledges to focus more on the economy and national security. To clinch the Republican nomination, he must outmaneuver Senators Marco Rubio, Ted Cruz, and Rand Paul, as well as former Hewlett-Packard CEO Carly Fiorina and retired neurosurgeon Ben Carson. Though Jeb Bush has yet to officially declare, he is considered the party's frontrunner.

text: The fact that a record-equalling 10 Wales players have been selected to start the British and Irish Lions' crucial final Test against Australia is a source of great national pride. Head coach Warren Gatland has opted to rely on familiar faces from his time coaching Wales, a team that claimed the Grand Slam in 2012, triumphed over England in the final game to secure this year's Six Nations title, and reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2011. Gatland's intimate knowledge of these players' capabilities, however, comes with its own set of pressures. Victory would cement his status as a hero, but a loss would likely lead to criticism for his heavy reliance on Welsh talent. This decision also intensifies the pressure on the Welsh players to deliver strong performances.All team selections inherently carry some risk, but it is somewhat unexpected to see five changes made for the second Test and another six for the Sydney Test. Typically, successful teams maintain stability rather than frequent alterations. Gatland's choice for the front row appears robust, although I find England lock Geoff Parling's retention in the second row rather fortunate. Personally, I would have included another Welshman, flanker Justin Tipuric, in the starting lineup.The Welsh players have additional motivation due to their recent poor record against Australia, having suffered eight consecutive losses. Despite this, Wales has been unlucky in their recent matches against the Wallabies and could have easily won two of their last three encounters. With these defeats fresh in their minds, they are eager for revenge.It is surprising to see Ireland centre Brian O'Driscoll excluded, as he would have been an ideal captain. However, Wales lock Alun Wyn Jones is in excellent form and will undoubtedly lead by example. If Wales centre Jamie Roberts is fully fit upon his return this weekend, his ability to cross the gain line could be crucial. The lack of such a player was a significant issue last Saturday when the Lions failed to make any breaks. To overcome the Australians, we need someone who can propel us forward.While our regional sides have struggled in recent years, fortunately, the national team has remained consistent. Reflecting on the 1971 and 1974 Lions teams, which I was part of, there was a strong Welsh influence. The positivity from the national side can indeed carry over to the Lions, as it did in 1971 when we won the series in New Zealand and in 1974 when we remained unbeaten in South Africa. Hopefully, history will repeat itself for the Lions on Saturday.The last two games have been nail-biters, decided by two-point and one-point margins, and this one might also come down to the wire. It promises to be a closely contested match, with Australia perhaps starting as slight favorites.JPR Williams shared his insights with BBC Sport's Matt Monaghan.

text: Hospital beds in England may fill up with the elderly and vulnerable because of cuts to local authority social care funding, a top NHS figure has warned. In a letter to the Daily Telegraph, Nigel Edwards, head of the NHS Confederation, raised concerns about potential hospital bed shortages due to funding cuts. Edwards warned that individuals requiring medical treatment might be denied beds as a result of these reductions.In response, the Department of Health announced an additional £2 billion allocation to safeguard social care services. Despite health spending being protected in Chancellor George Osborne's Spending Review, councils in England face a daunting 27% reduction in central government funding over the next four years.Mr. Edwards, representing health service bodies in England, acknowledged the £2 billion interim solution to social care funding as a welcome relief to many. However, he cautioned that the funding constraints could still have a knock-on effect on the health service. In his letter, Edwards stated, Less support from council services will quickly lead to increased pressure on emergency services and hospitals. Hospital beds will be blocked for those who badly need care because the support services the elderly require after discharge will not be available.Key points from the Spending Review include: - A £81 billion cut from public spending over four years. - An average departmental cut of 19%, less than the expected 25%. - An additional £7 billion in welfare cuts, affecting incapacity, housing benefits, and tax credits. - A £1.8 billion increase in public sector pension employee contributions by 2014. - An accelerated rise in the state pension age. - A 7% cut for local councils starting April next year. - The introduction of a permanent bank levy. - Rail fares set to rise 3% above inflation from 2012.Edwards emphasized, When it comes to the care of the most vulnerable in our society, it really is essential that the NHS and local authorities are in it together. The Department of Health acknowledged the impact of social care on NHS demands. A spokeswoman explained, That's why we are strengthening programmes like re-ablement and the 30-day re-admission tariff, which will integrate hospital care with care in the community.She added, We have allocated an additional £2 billion by 2014-15. This extra boost, alongside an ambitious programme of efficiency, will ensure that there is enough funding available both to protect people's access to services and deliver new approaches to improve quality and outcomes. We expect local health and social care professionals will work together to ensure that the funding is spent on joint health and social care priorities and improve outcomes for everyone.Councillor David Rogers from the Local Government Association expressed skepticism about the sufficiency of the extra £2 billion, stating, Of course that is very welcome, but as part of what councils said to the government before the Spending Review, there's likely to be a gap over that same time of about £6 billion. So, there are still going to be difficulties. But I think that the important thing is to ensure that both councils and the NHS locally work increasingly closely together to provide the best service to our residents.On Thursday, critics voiced concerns over whether the £2 billion designated for social care, half of which is to come from a direct grant to local government, would reach its intended target. Jennifer Dixon, chief executive of the Nuffield Trust think tank, noted, The reality is that local authority budgets will be stretched and funds for social care are not ring-fenced, so the extra £1 billion per year is by no means certain.

text: Antrim lost 2-06 to 0-09 to Limerick in their All-Ireland Qualifier Round 1B game at Corrigan Park on Saturday. Limerick, having not secured a competitive win all year, finally broke their streak with an impressive victory, fueled by early goals from Ian Ryan and Sean McSweeney, the latter from a penalty. By halftime, they led 2-2 to 0-6, with further points from McSweeney, Ryan, and Stephen Cahill sealing the win. Goalkeeper Donal O'Sullivan's heroics were crucial, as he made three vital saves to secure Limerick's triumph.Antrim's hopes of advancing in the championship were dashed, marking a disappointing end to their campaign after their promotion to Division Three of the Football League. They initially capitalized on the wind advantage, with Ryan Murphy scoring a free within 40 seconds and Kevin Niblock adding another from the right, giving them an early 0-2 to 0-0 lead.However, Limerick quickly turned the tide. Seanie Buckley found Ryan at the edge of the square, and the St Senan's player netted a low shot past Chris Kerr just five minutes in. Moments later, McSweeney converted a penalty after Darragh Treacy was fouled, driving the ball into the bottom right corner and pushing Limerick ahead 2-01 to 0-02.Despite Limerick's momentum, Antrim responded. Matthew Fitzpatrick scored from the right in the 13th minute, reducing the gap, and Patrick McBride added another four minutes later. Limerick's Tommy Childs, stepping in for injured captain Iain Corbett, impressed by setting up a fine score for Ryan after 18 minutes.Ryan had another chance for a second goal, but Kerr's quick reflexes denied him. Antrim closed the first half strongly, with McBride and Sean Burke narrowing Limerick's lead to two points at halftime.With a two-point advantage and a favorable wind, Limerick started the second half energetically. Cahill extended their lead to three in the 44th minute. Antrim, struggling to score, needed a goal to mount a comeback. Martin Johnson's attempt was thwarted by O'Sullivan's superb save.The introduction of Tomas McCann injected pace into Antrim's attack. He and Ryan Murray scored frees, cutting Limerick's lead to two points with nine minutes left. Ryan extended it back to a goal with another free. Antrim came close to scoring twice in the closing stages, but O'Sullivan's excellent saves against Murray and Johnson ensured Limerick's progression to the next round.Limerick's lineup included D O'Sullivan; P Browne, S Cahill (0-1), S O'Dea; B Fanning, J McCarthy, P Ranahan; D Treacy, S Buckley; G Noonan, P Nash, T Childs; S McSweeney (1-3, 1-0 pen, 0-3f), I Ryan (1-2), H Bourke. text: Saturday's FA Cup final between Arsenal and Aston Villa at Wembley will be watched by half a billion viewers in more than 120 countries. Nearly 90,000 fans are set to converge on Wembley for the 134th final of the world's oldest cup competition, where two teams of elite, millionaire athletes will vie for glory. Yet, what was the scene like at the inaugural final back in 1872?In stark contrast, an estimated 2,000 spectators gathered to witness 22 amateur players compete on a cricket pitch devoid of nets, as Wanderers triumphed over Royal Engineers 1-0, courtesy of Morton Betts' goal. BBC Sport, with insights from Matthew Taylor, a history professor at De Montfort University, revisits the first final held 143 years ago.Before the 1872 FA Cup, regular competitive football was nonexistent in England. Charles Alcock, the Football Association secretary, devised plans for the inaugural FA Cup, drawing 15 teams to the first round in November 1871. Among the participants were Barnes, Civil Service, Hitchin, Crystal Palace (not the current team, but a precursor dissolved in 1876), Maidenhead, Marlow, Queen's Park, Donington School, Upton Park, Clapham Rovers, Royal Engineers, Reigate Priory, Wanderers, Harrow Chequers, and Hampstead Heathens, who received a bye.Organizing football matches across Britain during the steam era presented logistical challenges, allowing Scottish side Queen's Park to reach the semi-finals without playing a match. Both semi-finals, ending in goalless draws, were held at Kennington Oval. The Royal Engineers secured a place in the final with a 3-0 replay victory over Crystal Palace, while Wanderers advanced after Queen's Park withdrew, unable to afford another trip to London.According to historians, the FA Cup was inspired by knockout competitions at major public schools like Harrow, though Alcock might have also drawn from regional competitions such as Sheffield's Youdan Cup, launched in 1867. Football was as established in Sheffield as in London, with elite ex-public schoolboys from the capital familiar with teams from Sheffield, Nottingham, and beyond.Alcock, the mastermind behind the FA Cup, played defense for Wanderers. Founded in 1859 as Forest Football Club, the team consisted mainly of former Harrow schoolboys and adopted the name 'Wanderers' due to their nomadic playing locations. By 1869, they were based at Kennington Oval, where Alcock also served as the secretary of Surrey cricket club.The Royal Engineers, established in 1863 by Major Francis Marindin, boasted a remarkable history. Marindin, a Crimean War veteran, played in the 1872 final, became FA president in 1874, and refereed eight more FA Cup finals.The 1872 final took place at Kennington Oval, which also hosted the first international football match between England and Scotland in 1870. The Oval would host 20 of the next 21 FA Cup finals, with the 1873 final held at Lillie Bridge near Chelsea's modern home, Stamford Bridge.Many football clubs in the late 19th century played on cricket grounds, emerging from cricket clubs as a way for players to stay fit during winter. Purpose-built football grounds didn't become common until the 1880s and 1890s.While today's fans face the bustling crowds at Wembley, the 1872 final was a more subdued affair, with football yet to gain widespread popularity. Around 2,000 spectators attended the Oval, with ticket prices at one shilling (equivalent to five pence today) deterring larger crowds. The audience was described as 'very fashionable', likely comprising the well-to-do, upper middle-class, and those connected to the public school network running the Football Association.The Royal Engineers were akin to the Barcelona of their era, pioneering the tactic of passing the ball to teammates, a stark contrast to the prevailing style of chasing the ball into space. The final's only goal came 15 minutes in, when Betts, under the alias A H Chequer from his Harrow Chequers club affiliation, scored after a long dribble by Walpole Vidal.Goalkeeping was not a specialized position, with players often alternating between field and goal roles. Teams frequently fielded six or seven forwards, relying on individual dribbling with teammates supporting the dribbler to advance the ball.The footballers of Oscar Wilde's era were a unique breed compared to today's stars. This case marked the first enforcement of the agreement, requiring Barker to pay a fine, attend a course, and perform community service with a civil rights organization.Kevin Kish, DFEH's director, told the BBC that Barker approached mediation with a willingness to contribute, which facilitated innovative solutions. text: At one of the shops serving the troops in Camp Bastion there are plenty of reminders that this war is nearly over, at least for those who have travelled from Britain and America. The shelves are looking sparse, with fewer goods available for purchase. Some remaining items boast special offers, while souvenirs maintain their full price, signaling an impending conclusion. Among these are drinking glasses with the phrase Been there; Done that, and a mug proclaiming Happiness is Helmand in the rear view mirror.Once a thriving military hub akin to the size of Reading, Bastion is now transforming into a ghost town. Compounds that previously bustled with tents and military vehicles now stand empty. The sight of uniformed men and women has dwindled, and the once-frequent helicopter blades slicing the air now sound only intermittently.As Bastion contracts, nearly all other British bases in Helmand have already vanished. During the war's peak, around 10,000 British military personnel were stationed at 137 bases across southern Afghanistan. Today, approximately 4,000 UK personnel remain at just two locations: the main base at Bastion and an observation post named Sterga 2, which offers a strategic view over the Helmand valley.In the upcoming months, Sterga will transition to NATO command, with the British-led Task Force Helmand integrating into Regional Command South West under the leadership of a US Marine Corps brigadier general. Lashkar Gah, once a main operating base and the former British headquarters, has already been handed over to Afghan control. The buildings that housed a British provincial reconstruction team are set to become a health center, though no UK personnel will be present to witness the change.Make no mistake: this marks a full withdrawal by the British from one of Afghanistan's most violent regions. Camp Price, once home to 2,000 troops, has been dismantled in recent weeks. Chainsaws and diggers have become the new tools for British soldiers, tearing down the protective Hesco walls and leveling the ground. Even concrete barriers, once makeshift memorials with graffiti honoring fallen comrades, have been removed.As Capt. David Goodman oversees the last shipping containers being loaded onto trucks, he reflects on the logistics of the operation. Since October, 600 containers have departed from Price. I am now dreaming of ISO containers, he says. Sending out 20 or 30 a day has been a nightmare, waking up wondering 'did this container go?'Little has been left behind, prompting questions about the British forces' lasting legacy after eight years in Helmand and 448 military deaths. Peace is certainly not the legacy, as gunfire still echoes in the distance while the last containers are loaded at Camp Price.Lt. Col. Mike Caldicott of the Royal Logistic Corps led the final military convoy out of Price, likely one of the last logistic patrols in Helmand. He believes they have made a difference. I only wish people at home could see the changes I've seen, he says. I think they'd feel better about our investment.This sentiment contrasts with some soldiers who are more focused on returning home than reflecting on their impact. One soldier simply states, Job done, get home. Another adds, I will miss the sun, that's probably about it.While many soldiers feel they have made a difference, few echo David Cameron's claim from last year that the mission is accomplished. Lt. Gen. John Lorimer, the highest-ranking British general in Afghanistan, acknowledges extraordinary things have been achieved across the country. However, when asked if it is mission accomplished, he avoids the phrase, saying instead, There is still a lot to be done. A senior British officer compares Afghanistan to a PhD, while Iraq was merely an A-level exam.Back home, the sentiment is more somber. Public weariness of war is evident in the current hesitance regarding military intervention. Margaret Evison, who lost her only son Mark in Helmand in 2009, says she has come to terms with her loss but questions the justification for her son's death. She is uncertain if the British withdrawal coincides with a more stable Afghanistan. Regarding Cameron's mission accomplished assertion, she remarks, Well, he has to say that!Brig. James Woodham, the final commander of Task Force Helmand, agrees there is still much work to be done. He acknowledges progress but admits, Ultimately, history will be the judge of what has been achieved.It is peculiar that after eight years of investment, there will soon be no British military presence to help write the final chapter in Helmand.

text: Basketball's biggest star LeBron James has announced his return to the Cleveland Cavaliers - the team where he began his NBA career 11 years ago. In an exclusive interview with Sports Illustrated on Friday, 29-year-old LeBron James announced his return to the Cleveland Cavaliers. James, who became a free agent on July 1 after opting out of the final two years of his Miami Heat contract, shared his long-held desire to end his career in Cleveland. I always believed I'd return to Cleveland and finish my career there, he stated.Having been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times, James left Miami last month, forgoing $42.7 million (£25.1 million) he would have earned over the next two years. His decision ignited a frenzy among teams eager to secure him, but James revealed that a return to his home state of Ohio was always foremost in his mind. After last season, free agency wasn't even a thought, said James, who hails from Akron, just 40 miles from Cleveland. But I have two boys, and my wife, Savannah, is pregnant with a girl. I started thinking about what it would be like to raise my family in my hometown.James considered other teams but admitted, I wasn't going to leave Miami for anywhere except Cleveland. The more time passed, the more it felt right. This is what makes me happy. James' journey began with the Cavaliers as the first draft pick in 2003, where he became a superstar over seven years before joining Miami in 2010. There, he formed a formidable trio with Chris Bosh and Dwyane Wade. His departure to Miami, announced during an ESPN special titled The Decision, sparked outrage among Cleveland fans, who burned his jerseys in protest.During his tenure with the Heat, James, who would have earned $20 million (£11.7 million) next season, clinched NBA titles in 2012 and 2013 and led the team to the Finals in 2011 and 2014. Reflecting on his Miami experience, James remarked, The hardest thing to leave is what I built with those guys. I've talked to some of them and will talk to others. Nothing will ever change what we accomplished. We are brothers for life.The news of James' return was broadcasted over the loudspeaker at Cleveland airport, causing Cavaliers ticket phone lines to crash, according to ESPN. In 2010, Cavaliers owner Dan Gilbert had penned an open letter criticizing James, labeling his departure a shocking act of disloyalty and a shameful display of selfishness and betrayal. However, on Friday, Gilbert tweeted, My eight-year-old: 'Daddy, does this mean I can finally wear my LeBron jersey, again?' Yes it does, son. Yes it does!Meanwhile, in Miami, a mural of James was defaced, as reported by South Florida news station WPLG Local 10. Heat owner Micky Arison expressed his sentiments on Twitter: I am shocked and disappointed in today's news. However, I will never forget what LeBron brought us for four years. Thanks for the memories.The Heat's situation could worsen, as Wade and Bosh, who also opted for free agency this summer, might follow James' lead and leave Miami. Alongside the Sports Illustrated interview, James posted a photo on Instagram donning a Cavaliers uniform with the caption, I'm coming home. Despite the excitement, he cautioned Cleveland fans not to expect immediate triumphs. When I left Cleveland, I was on a mission, James explained. I was seeking championships, and we won two. But Miami already knew that feeling. Our city hasn't had that feeling in a long, long, long time.I'm not promising a championship. I know how hard that is to deliver, James added. We're not ready right now. No way. Of course, I want to win next year, but I'm realistic. It will be a long process, much longer than it was in 2010. My patience will get tested. I know that.
